{"parentUuid":"0a3af407-27e0-4731-a8a3-7f7ad4ca19c3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_yu5uk3juq7tb02ja99n7xuzm","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/crc.rs","content":"//! CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320).\n//!\n//! Used as an end-to-end integrity tag on the file header and on every page so\n//! that torn writes / injected bit flips are detected on read-back rather than\n//! silently interpreted as live data.\n\n/// Update a running CRC-32 with `bytes`. Start with `0u32`, and finalize with\n/// `CRC ^= 0xFFFF_FFFF`.\npub fn update(mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    crc ^= 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n    for &b in bytes {\n        crc ^= b as u32;\n        for _ in 0..8 {\n            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(crc & 1)));\n        }\n    }\n    crc ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n}\n\n/// One-shot CRC-32 over the whole slice.\npub fn checksum(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    update(0, bytes)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"\"), 0x0000_0000);\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"123456789\"), 0xCBF4_3926);\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"a\"), 0xE8B7_BE43);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn streaming_matches_oneshot() {\n        let data = b\"the quick brown fox\";\n        let mut c = update(0, &data[..5]);\n        c = update_pre(c, &data[5..]);\n        // update() restarts; emulate continuation by raw loop:\n        fn raw(mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n            for &b in bytes {\n                crc ^= b as u32;\n                for _ in 0..8 {\n                    crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(crc & 1)));\n                }\n            }\n            crc\n        }\n        let expect = {\n            let c = raw(0xFFFF_FFFF ^ 0, &data[..5]);\n            raw(c, &data[5..]) ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n        };\n        assert_eq!(c, expect);\n    }\n\n    fn update_pre(crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        // continuation variant (no re-init)\n        let mut c = crc ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n        for &b in bytes {\n            c ^= b as u32;\n            for _ in 0..8 {\n                c = (c >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(c & 1)));\n            }\n        }\n        c ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_4d6885725e87e67dbdd3f995","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":3115,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":26424,"output_tokens":989,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"ad18fc0d-7410-4910-86f1-b5bb8c9c9b34","timestamp":"2026-09-22T15:56:03.839Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320).\n//!\n//! Used as an end-to-end integrity tag on the file header and on every page so\n//! that torn writes / injected bit flips are detected on read-back rather than\n//! silently interpreted as live data.\n\n/// Update a running CRC-32 with `bytes`. Start with `0u32`, and finalize with\n/// `CRC ^= 0xFFFF_FFFF`.\npub fn update(mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    crc ^= 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n    for &b in bytes {\n        crc ^= b as u32;\n        for _ in 0..8 {\n            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(crc & 1)));\n        }\n    }\n    crc ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n}\n\n/// One-shot CRC-32 over the whole slice.\npub fn checksum(bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    update(0, bytes)\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"\"), 0x0000_0000);\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"123456789\"), 0xCBF4_3926);\n        assert_eq!(checksum(b\"a\"), 0xE8B7_BE43);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn streaming_matches_oneshot() {\n        let data = b\"the quick brown fox\";\n        let mut c = update(0, &data[..5]);\n        c = update_pre(c, &data[5..]);\n        // update() restarts; emulate continuation by raw loop:\n        fn raw(mut crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n            for &b in bytes {\n                crc ^= b as u32;\n                for _ in 0..8 {\n                    crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(crc & 1)));\n                }\n            }\n            crc\n        }\n        let expect = {\n            let c = raw(0xFFFF_FFFF ^ 0, &data[..5]);\n            raw(c, &data[5..]) ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n        };\n        assert_eq!(c, expect);\n    }\n\n    fn update_pre(crc: u32, bytes: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n        // continuation variant (no re-init)\n        let mut c = crc ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF;\n        for &b in bytes {\n            c ^= b as u32;\n            for _ in 0..8 {\n                c = (c >> 1) ^ (0xEDB8_8320 & (0u32.wrapping_sub(c & 1)));\n            }\n        }\n        c ^ 0xFFFF_FFFF\n    }\n}\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"969c7df8-fd7c-4093-bc52-f7a100a10ae6","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

Injectable I/O layer.\n//!\n//! All disk access goes through the [`Storage`] trait. Two real implementations\n//! are provided ([`FileStorage`], backed by an `std::fs::File`, and\n//! [`MemStorage`], an in-memory vector), plus [`FaultyStorage`], a decorator\n//! that injects failures and byte corruption on demand. The allocator itself is\n//! generic over `Storage`, so the very same code paths used against a real file\n//! can be driven through simulated faults in tests.\n//!\n//! ## Sync boundary\n//!\n//! The repository persists exactly one page (or the file header) per\n//! [`Storage::write`] call, and [`Storage::sync`] maps to `fsync`\n//! (`File::sync_all`). A logical mutation is therefore:\n//!\n//! 1. modify the in-memory page;\n//! 2. one `write` of the whole fixed-size page to its deterministic offset;\n//! 3. optionally one `sync`.\n//!\n//! No operation spans multiple page writes (compaction rewrites only the page\n//! it compacts), so a single page write + checksum is the crash-atomicity\n//! unit. A torn write is detected by the per-page CRC on the next open.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\n/// Random-access block device with a fixed block size and explicit sync.\npub trait Storage: Send {\n    /// Block (page) size in bytes.\n    fn block_size(&self) -> u32;\n\n    /// File length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> u64;\n\n    /// Is the backing storage empty (zero bytes)?\n    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Read `block_size` bytes for block index `block_no` into `buf`.\n    /// Returns an error if the block is past end of file or is short.\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n\n    /// Write exactly `buf.len()` bytes at block index `block_no`, extending the\n    /// file if needed. `buf` is exactly one block.\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n\n    /// Persist previously written data to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Real, file-backed storage. Block 0 is reserved for the file header; page\n/// `pid` lives at byte offset `header_size + pid * block_size`.\npub struct FileStorage {\n    file: File,\n    block_size: u32,\n    len: u64,\n}\n\nimpl FileStorage {\n    /// Open (creating if absent) the file at `path`.\n    pub fn open(path: &Path, block_size: u32) -> io::Result<Self> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(path)?;\n        let len = file.metadata()?.len();\n        Ok(Self {\n            file,\n            block_size,\n            len,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Storage for FileStorage {\n    fn block_size(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.block_size\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.len\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = block_no as u64 * self.block_size as u64;\n        if offset + self.block_size as u64 > self.len {\n            return Err(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof,\n                format!(\"block {block_no} past end of file (len {})\", self.len),\n            ));\n        }\n        self.file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        self.file.read_exact(buf)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = block_no as u64 * self.block_size as u64;\n        self.file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        self.file.write_all(buf)?;\n        self.len = self.len.max(offset + buf.len() as u64);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.file.sync_all()\n    }\n}\n\n/// In-memory storage — fast path for tests and for the reference checks.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct MemStorage {\n    data: Vec<u8>,\n    block_size: u32,\n}\n\nimpl MemStorage {\n    pub fn new(block_size: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            data: Vec::new(),\n            block_size,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Storage for MemStorage {\n    fn block_size(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.block_size\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.data.len() as u64\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = block_no as usize * self.block_size as usize;\n        if offset + buf.len() > self.data.len() {\n            return Err(io::Error::new(\n                io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof,\n                format!(\"block {block_no} past end of memory file\"),\n            ));\n        }\n        buf.copy_from_slice(&self.data[offset..offset + buf.len()]);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = block_no as usize * self.block_size as usize;\n        if offset + buf.len() > self.data.len() {\n            self.data.resize(offset + buf.len(), 0);\n        }\n        self.data[offset..offset + buf.len()].copy_from_slice(buf);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Which underlying operation a scheduled fault applies to.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultOp {\n    Read,\n    Write,\n    Sync,\n}\n\n/// One scheduled fault: after the inner storage sees `after` matching\n/// operations of kind `op` (or on the *next* matching operation when `after` is\n/// 0), inject the behaviour.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Fault {\n    pub op: FaultOp,\n    /// 0 = the next matching op, n = after n further matching ops have\n    /// succeeded.\n    pub after: u32,\n    pub kind: FaultKind,\n}\n\n/// How the fault manifests.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum FaultKind {\n    /// Fail the syscall with an `IoError` carrying this message.\n    Error(String),\n    /// Let the write go through but flip the lowest bit of byte `byte_offset`\n    /// within the block, simulating a silently corrupted/torn page.\n    CorruptBit { byte_offset: usize },\n}\n\n/// Decorator that injects [`Fault`]s into an inner [`Storage`].\n///\n/// Faults are matched in insertion order against the operation stream. The\n/// fault policy is behind a mutex so the same policy can be scheduled from a\n/// test while the allocator owns the storage.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct FaultyStorage {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn Storage + Send>>>,\n    block_size: u32,\n    policy: Arc<Mutex<FaultPolicy>>,\n}\n\n/// Mutable schedule of pending faults, plus a log of operations observed.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct FaultPolicy {\n    /// Pending faults in schedule order.\n    pub faults: Vec<Fault>,\n    /// Flat log of observed ops (oldest first).\n    pub log: Vec<FaultOp>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultPolicy {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    pub fn schedule(&mut self, fault: Fault) {\n        self.faults.push(fault);\n    }\n\n    /// Shortcut: fail the next matching operation.\n    pub fn fail_next(&mut self, op: FaultOp, msg: impl Into<String>) {\n        self.schedule(Fault {\n            op,\n            after: 0,\n            kind: FaultKind::Error(msg.into()),\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Shortcut: corrupt a byte in the next matching write.\n    pub fn corrupt_next_write(&mut self, byte_offset: usize) {\n        self.schedule(Fault {\n            op: FaultOp::Write,\n            after: 0,\n            kind: FaultKind::CorruptBit { byte_offset },\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Number of matching ops observed so far.\n    pub fn count(&self, op: FaultOp) -> usize {\n        self.log.iter().filter(|o| **o == op).count()\n    }\n\n    fn take_effect(&mut self, op: FaultOp) -> Option<FaultKind> {\n        self.log.push(op);\n        // Consume the first pending fault for this op whose counter is due.\n        for (i, f) in self.faults.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n            if f.op != op {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if f.after == 0 {\n                let Fault { kind, .. } = self.faults.remove(i);\n                return Some(kind);\n            }\n            f.after -= 1;\n        }\n        None\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FaultyStorage {\n    /// Wrap any storage. Keep the returned policy handle to schedule faults\n    /// from outside.\n    pub fn wrap<S: Storage + Send + 'static>(inner: S) -> (Self, Arc<Mutex<FaultPolicy>>) {\n        let block_size = inner.block_size();\n        let policy = Arc::new(Mutex::new(FaultPolicy::new()));\n        (\n            Self {\n                inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Box::new(inner))),\n                block_size,\n                policy: Arc::clone(&policy),\n            },\n            policy,\n        )\n    }\n\n    pub fn policy(&self) -> Arc<Mutex<FaultPolicy>> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.policy)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Storage for FaultyStorage {\n    fn block_size(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.block_size\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().len()\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(kind) = self.policy.lock().unwrap().take_effect(FaultOp::Read) {\n            if let FaultKind::Error(msg) = kind {\n                return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Io, msg));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().read_block(block_no, buf)\n    }\n\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let effect = self.policy.lock().unwrap().take_effect(FaultOp::Write);\n        if let Some(kind) = effect {\n            match kind {\n                FaultKind::Error(msg) => return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Io, msg)),\n                FaultKind::CorruptBit { byte_offset } => {\n                    let mut damaged = buf.to_vec();\n                    if let Some(b) = damaged.get_mut(byte_offset) {\n                        *b ^= 0x01;\n                    }\n                    return self.inner.lock().unwrap().write_block(block_no, &damaged);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().write_block(block_no, buf)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(kind) = self.policy.lock().unwrap().take_effect(FaultOp::Sync) {\n            if let FaultKind::Error(msg) = kind {\n                return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Io, msg));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().sync()\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_8138f9c8d747ef1208479a14","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":744,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":30520,"output_tokens":3089,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"72f82d32-b3d0-4bf6-a78e-b491bda069df","timestamp":"2026-09-22T15:57:20.193Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

A torn write is detected by the per-page CRC on the next open.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\n/// Random-access block device with a fixed block size and explicit sync.\npub trait Storage: Send {\n    /// Block (page) size in bytes.\n    fn block_size(&self) -> u32;\n\n    /// File length in bytes.\n    fn len(&self) -> u64;\n\n    /// Is the backing storage empty (zero bytes)?\n    fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Read `block_size` bytes for block index `block_no` into `buf`.\n    /// Returns an error if the block is past end of file or is short.\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n\n    /// Write exactly `buf.len()` bytes at block index `block_no`, extending the\n    /// file if needed. `buf` is exactly one block.\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n\n    /// Persist previously written data to stable storage (`fsync`).\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Real, file-backed storage. Block 0 is reserved for the file header; page\n/// `pid` lives at byte offset `header_size + pid * block_size`.\npub struct FileStorage {\n    file: File,\n    block_size: u32,\n    len: u64,\n}\n\nimpl FileStorage {\n    /// Open (creating if absent) the file at `path`.\n    pub fn open(path: &Path, block_size: u32) -> io::Result<Self> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(path)?;\n        let len = file.metadata()?.len();\n        Ok(Self {\n {\n        self.len\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn write_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), self.block_size as usize);\n        let offset = block_no as u64 * Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Which underlying operation a scheduled fault applies to.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultOp {\n    Read,\n    Write,\n    Sync,\n}\n\n/// One kind: FaultKind::Error(msg.into()),\n        });\n    }\n\n    /// Shortcut: corrupt a byte in the next matching write.\n    pub fn corrupt_next_write(&mut self, byte_offset: usize) {\n so far.\n    pub fn count(&self, op: FaultOp) -> usize {\n        self.log.iter().filter(|o| **o == op).count()\n    }\n\n    fn take_effect(&mut self, op: FaultOp) -> Option<FaultKind> {\n        self.log.push(op);\n        // Consume the first pending fault for this op whose counter is due.\n        for (i, f) in self.faults.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n            if f.op != op {\n 1;\n        }\n        None\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FaultyStorage {\n    /// Wrap any storage. inner.block_size();\n        let policy = Arc::new(Mutex::new(FaultPolicy::new()));\n        (\n            Self {\n                inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Box::new(inner))),\n self.inner.lock().unwrap().len()\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&mut self, block_no: u32, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        if let Some(kind) = Variable-length record page: the slotted-page allocator with an explicit\n//! free-space region made of disjoint intervals.\n//!\n//! # On-disk page format (fixed size `block_size` bytes)\n//!\n//! ```text\n//!  offset 0            page header (16 bytes)\n//!  offset 16           slot directory: slot_count * 12 bytes (grows upward)\n//!                      ... free data region ...\n//!                      live records (packed toward the end by compact)\n//!  offset bs-4         CRC-32 over bytes [0 .. bs-4)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Header:\n//! - `u32` magic `PAGE_MAGIC`\n//! - `u32` page id (must match the index at which the page was read)\n//! - `u16` slot_count   (directory entries, dead or alive)\n//! - `u16` free_count   (number of free intervals rebuilt on load; integrity check)\n//! - `u32` crc32 of `[0, bs-4)`\n//!\n//! Slot entry (12 bytes, little-endian):\n//! - `u16` offset  — byte offset of the record (0 while the slot is dead)\n//! - `u16` length  — record length; **0 means dead/freeable slot**\n//! - `u32` generation — monotonically increasing per-slot generation; the\n//!   value clients must present. Incremented on every free.\n//!\n//! The free intervals themselves are *not* persisted: on load they are rebuilt\n//! from the live slots and their count is compared with the stored\n//! `free_count` so corruption manifests as an error instead of silently\n//! changing free space accounting.\n//!\n//! # Invariants (checked by [`Page::verify_partition`])\n//!\n//! - Every live record lies inside the data region `[16+12*n, bs-4)`.\n//! - Live records are pairwise disjoint.\n//! - Free intervals are pairwise disjoint, interior-disjoint from live\n//!   records, and their union plus live records exactly equals the data\n//!   region — i.e. no overlaps and no missing space (space conservation).\n\nuse crate::crc;\nuse crate::err::{Error, Result};\n\n/// Page header length.\npub const PAGE_HEADER_LEN: u32 = 16;\n/// One slot-directory entry.\npub const SLOT_LEN: u32 = 12;\n/// Magic prefix of every formatted page.\npub const PAGE_MAGIC: u32 = 0x5046_4131; // \"PFA1\"\n\n/// One directory entry.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Slot {\n    pub off: u16,\n    pub len: u16,\n    pub gen: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Slot {\n    const DEAD: Slot = Slot {\n        off: 0,\n        len: 0,\n        gen: 0,\n    };\n\n    fn encode(&self, out: &mut [u8]) {\n        out[0..2].copy_from_slice(&self.off.to_le_bytes());\n        out[2..4].copy_from_slice(&self.len.to_le_bytes());\n        out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&self.gen.to_le_bytes());\n        out[8..12].fill(0);\n    }\n\n    fn decode(raw: &[u8]) -> Slot {\n        Slot {\n            off: u16::from_le_bytes([raw[0], raw[1]]),\n            len: u16::from_le_bytes([raw[2], raw[3]]),\n            gen: u32::from_le_bytes([raw[4], raw[5], raw[6], raw[7]]),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Half-open byte interval `[start, start+len)` inside the data region.\npub type Interval = (u16, u16);\n\n/// One mutable page image.\npub struct Page {\n    pid: u32,\n    block_size: u32,\n    slots: Vec<Slot>,\n    /// Free data intervals, disjoint, sorted ascending by offset.\n    free: Vec<Interval>,\n    /// Serialized page bytes (header + directory + records); always kept\n    /// consistent with `slots`/`free` after each mutation.\n    raw: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl Page {\n    /// First byte of the data region (immediately after the directory).\n    fn data_start(&self) -> u16 {\n        (PAGE_HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN * self.slots.len() as u32) as u16\n    }\n\n    /// One byte past the last data byte (CRC trailer begins here).\n    fn data_end(&self) -> u16 {\n        (self.block_size - 4) as u16\n    }\n\n    /// Total bytes of data-region free space.\n    pub fn free_bytes(&self) -> usize {\n        self.free.iter().map(|(_, l)| *l as usize).sum()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of free intervals (fragmentation indicator).\n    pub fn free_interval_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.free.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of directory entries (including dead ones).\n    pub fn slot_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.slots.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Number of live records.\n    pub fn live_count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.slots.iter().filter(|s| s.len != 0).count()\n    }\n\n    pub fn pid(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.pid\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_size(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.block_size\n    }\n\n    /// Format a fresh, empty page.\n    pub fn format(pid: u32, block_size: u32) -> Result<Page> {\n        validate_block_size(block_size)?;\n        let mut page = Page {\n            pid,\n            block_size,\n            slots: Vec::new(),\n            free: Vec::new(),\n            raw: vec![0u8; block_size as usize],\n        };\n        page.rebuild_free();\n        page.sync_header_and_crc();\n        Ok(page)\n    }\n\n    /// Decode and validate a page image read from storage.\n    pub fn decode(pid_expected: u32, raw: &[u8], block_size: u32) -> Result<Page> {\n        validate_block_size(block_size)?;\n        if raw.len() != block_size as usize {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page {pid_expected}: block has {} bytes, expected {block_size}\",\n                raw.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        let stored_crc = u32::from_le_bytes([\n            raw[block_size as usize - 4],\n            raw[block_size as usize - 3],\n            raw[block_size as usize - 2],\n            raw[block_size as usize - 1],\n        ]);\n        let actual_crc = crc::checksum(&raw[..block_size as usize - 4]);\n        if stored_crc != actual_crc {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page {pid_expected}: CRC mismatch (stored {stored_crc:#010x}, computed {actual_crc:#010x})\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let magic = u32::from_le_bytes([raw[0], raw[1], raw[2], raw[3]]);\n        if magic != PAGE_MAGIC {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page {pid_expected}: bad magic {magic:#010x}\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let pid = u32::from_le_bytes([raw[4], raw[5], raw[6], raw[7]]);\n        if pid != pid_expected {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page header id {pid} != block index {pid_expected}\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let slot_count = u16::from_le_bytes([raw[8], raw[9]]) as usize;\n        let free_count = u16::from_le_bytes([raw[10], raw[11]]) as usize;\n\n        let dir_end = PAGE_HEADER_LEN as usize + SLOT_LEN as usize * slot_count;\n        if dir_end > block_size as usize - 4 {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page {pid}: slot_count {slot_count} overruns page\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(slot_count);\n        for i in 0..slot_count {\n            let base = PAGE_HEADER_LEN as usize + i * SLOT_LEN as usize;\n            slots.push(Slot::decode(&raw[base..base + SLOT_LEN as usize]));\n        }\n        let mut page = Page {\n            pid,\n            block_size,\n            slots,\n            free: Vec::new(),\n            raw: raw.to_vec(),\n        };\n        page.rebuild_free();\n        page.verify_partition()?;\n        if page.free.len() != free_count {\n            return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                \"page {pid}: rebuilt {} free intervals but header says {free_count}\",\n                page.free.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(page)\n    }\n\n    /// Current serialized image (header, directory, records, CRC trailer).\n    pub fn encode(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        &self.raw\n    }\n\n    /// Rebuild the free interval list from scratch: start with the whole data\n    /// region free, then subtract every live record, splitting as required.\n    fn rebuild_free(&mut self) {\n        let ds = self.data_start();\n        let de = self.data_end();\n        let mut taken: Vec<Interval> = self\n            .slots\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.len != 0)\n            .map(|s| (s.off, s.len))\n            .collect();\n        taken.sort_unstable_by_key(|(o, _)| *o);\n\n        let mut free: Vec<Interval> = vec![(ds, de - ds)];\n        for (off, len) in taken {\n            let end = off as u32 + len as u32;\n            let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(free.len() + 1);\n            for (fs, fl) in free {\n                let fend = fs as u32 + fl as u32;\n                if end <= fs as u32 || off as u32 >= fend {\n                    next.push((fs, fl)); // disjoint\n                } else {\n                    // record lies (partly) inside this interval; split around it\n                    if off > fs {\n                        next.push((fs, (off as u32 - fs as u32) as u16));\n                    }\n                    if end < fend {\n                        next.push((end as u16, (fend - end) as u16));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            free = next;\n        }\n        free.sort_unstable_by_key(|(o, _)| *o);\n        self.free = free;\n    }\n\n    /// Check the full partition invariant; returns [`Error::Corrupt`] on any\n    /// overlap, out-of-bounds record, or conservation mismatch.\n    pub fn verify_partition(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let ds = self.data_start() as u32;\n        let de = self.data_end() as u32;\n\n        // Live records inside the data region and pairwise disjoint.\n        let mut lives: Vec<(u32, u32)> = self\n            .slots\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.len != 0)\n            .map(|s| {\n                let end = s.off as u32 + s.len as u32;\n                (s.off as u32, end)\n            })\n            .collect();\n        lives.sort_unstable();\n        let mut prev_end = ds;\n        for (start, end) in &lives {\n            if *start < ds || *end > de || start >= end {\n                return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                    \"page {}: record [{start},{end}) outside data region [{ds},{de})\",\n                    self.pid\n                )));\n            }\n            if *start < prev_end {\n                return Err(Error::Corrupt(format!(\n                    \"page {}: live records overlap at byte {start}\",\n                    self.pid\n                )));\n A slot's footprint is not remembered after death, so\n        // dead-slot reuse is driven purely by interval size: pick the smallest\n        // fitting interval; whether the directory needs to grow is independent.\n        let _ = dead;\n\n        // 2) Directory growth needs 12 extra bytes *and* `need` bytes in the\n        //    head interval (the one abutting the directory). Existing dead\n        //    slots avoid the 12-byte growth.\n        let dead_slot = self.slots.iter().position(|s| s.len == 0);\n\n        if let Some(si) = dead_slot {\n            if let Some(fi) = self.free.iter().position(|(_, l)| *l as u32 >= need) {\n                let (si_, gen_) = self.place_in_interval(si, fi, len)?;\n                return Ok((si_, gen_));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Grow directory: head free interval must start at data_start and\n        // contain SLOT_LEN + need bytes.\n        let head = self\n            .free\n            .iter()\n            .position(|(o, _)| *o as u32 == ds);","new_string":"        // Reuse a dead directory entry if one exists and some free interval\n        // fits the record. That\n        // growth is taken from the head free interval (the one abutting the\n        // directory), which must therefore also contain the record bytes.\n        let head = self\n            .free\n            .iter()\n            .position(|(o, _)| *o as u32 == ds);"},"name":"Edit","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_876c3dcfbfd7cba53e675c06","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":13530,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":24376,"output_tokens":4735,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"d0592cc8-84ce-4f41-be07-a90d32363149","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:02:54.672Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"d5768359-7f72-4721-91be-ceb11ac2bc26","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"signature":"","thinking":"Now there's one more subtle issue with dead slot reuse and generation.\n\nFree: gen G (live) -> slot gen becomes G+1 (dead).\nReuse: dead slot gen is G+1,\n\nI've verified that stale handles are correctly rejected under both free and reuse scenarios. {"parentUuid":"6d2d8139-2c56-4216-ac78-5254459fdafe","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_ci982xp9wg3sn7juq2r7dodu","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/err.rs","content":"//! Crate-wide error type.\n\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::io;\n\n/// Result alias used throughout the crate.\npub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;\n\n/// All fallible outcomes in the allocator.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum Error {\n    /// Underlying I/O failure (real disk or injected).\n    Io(io::Error),\n    /// Bad caller-supplied configuration.\n    BadConfig(String),\n    /// Malformed caller request (e.g. zero-length record, bad JSON).\n    BadRequest(String),\n    /// On-disk structure failed validation: CRC, magic, partition invariant.\n    Corrupt(String),\n    /// Record cannot fit on a page even accounting for the directory.\n    RecordTooLarge { len: usize, usable: usize },\n    /// No free interval on the target page fits the record.\n    OutOfSpace {\n        page: u32,\n        needed: usize,\n        free_total: usize,\n        largest: usize,\n        hint: String,\n    },\n    /// Handle references a slot index that never existed on this page.\n    NoSuchSlot { page: u32, slot: usize },\n    /// Handle generation no longer (or never) matched a live record:\n    /// use-after-free, double-free, or handle from a wiped page.\n    StaleHandle {\n        page: u32,\n        slot: usize,\n        presented_gen: u32,\n        current_gen: Option<u32>,\n    },\n    /// In-place write length differs from the allocated record length.\n    LengthMismatch { slot_len: usize, write_len: usize },\n    /// The reference model disagrees with the allocator (test-only invariant).\n    Model(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Error {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Error::Io(e) => write!(f, \"I/O error: {e}\"),\n            Error::BadConfig(m) => write!(f, \"bad configuration: {m}\"),\n            Error::BadRequest(m) => write!(f, \"bad request: {m}\"),\n            Error::Corrupt(m) => write!(f, \"corrupt storage: {m}\"),\n            Error::RecordTooLarge { len, usable } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"record of {len} bytes cannot fit a page with {usable} usable bytes\"\n            ),\n            Error::OutOfSpace {\n                page,\n                needed,\n                free_total,\n                largest,\n                hint,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"page {page} out of space: need {needed}, free total {free_total} in {largest} largest interval; {hint}\"\n            ),\n            Error::NoSuchSlot { page, slot } => {\n                write!(f, \"page {page} has no slot {slot}\")\n            }\n            Error::StaleHandle {\n                page,\n                slot,\n                presented_gen,\n                current_gen,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"stale handle (page {page}, slot {slot}, presented generation {presented_gen}, current {})\",\n                current_gen\n                    .map(|g| g.to_string())\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"dead\".into())\n            ),\n            Error::LengthMismatch {\n                slot_len,\n                write_len,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"in-place write of {write_len} bytes into a {slot_len}-byte record\"\n            ),\n            Error::Model(m) => write!(f, \"reference model violation: {m}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for Error {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            Error::Io(e) => Some(e),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for Error {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        Error::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_ae78bf4b97bb0f7694374bbd","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":951,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":41784,"output_tokens":2164,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"b11a9392-7ccd-409c-8d4e-10ebdba8ed1a","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:05:09.364Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"9482089f-972f-4c5e-ab25-6381deed30b6","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_01cku2oxidou7y737lfx7f2n","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/handle.rs","content":"//! Opaque record handles carrying a generation.\n//!\n//! A [`Handle`] names exactly one incarnation of one record:\n//! `(page id, slot index, generation)`. The slot index may be reused after the\n//! record is freed, but the generation advances on every free (and on reuse),\n//! so a handle kept past the free (use-after-free / double-free) is rejected\n//! instead of silently addressing whatever record later occupies the slot.\n//!\n//! External wire form: `p{page}.s{slot}.g{generation}` — short, unambiguous,\n//! and easy to paste into HTTP requests.\n\nuse crate::err::{Error, Result};\nuse std::fmt;\nuse std::str::FromStr;\n\n/// A client-held reference to one record incarnation.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]\npub struct Handle {\n    pub page: u32,\n    pub slot: u32,\n    pub gen: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Handle {\n    pub fn new(page: u32, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            page,\n            slot: slot as u32,\n            gen,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn slot_index(&self) -> usize {\n        self.slot as usize\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Handle {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        write!(f, \"p{}.s{}.g{}\", self.page, self.slot, self.gen)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromStr for Handle {\n    type Err = Error;\n\n    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let bad = || Error::BadRequest(format!(\"malformed handle {s:?}, expected p<page>.s<slot>.g<gen>\"));\n        let rest = s.strip_prefix('p').ok_or_else(bad)?;\n        let (pid, rest) = rest.split_once(\".s\").ok_or_else(bad)?;\n        let (slot, gen) = rest.split_once(\".g\").ok_or_else(bad)?;\n        Ok(Handle {\n            page: pid.parse().map_err(|_| bad())?,\n            slot: slot.parse().map_err(|_| bad())?,\n            gen: gen.parse().map_err(|_| bad())?,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn roundtrip() {\n        let h = Handle::new(7, 3, 42);\n        let s = h.to_string();\n        assert_eq!(s, \"p7.s3.g42\");\n        assert_eq!(s.parse::<Handle>().unwrap(), h);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_garbage() {\n        for s in [\"\", \"p1\", \"p1.s2\", \"x1.s2.g3\", \"pa.s2.g3\", \"p1.sb.g3\", \"p1.s2.gc\"] {\n            assert!(s.parse::<Handle>().is_err(), \"accepted {s:?}\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_ae78bf4b97bb0f7694374bbd","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":951,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":41784,"output_tokens":2164,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"05af0351-0d24-4add-8b04-05975dde7a30","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:05:09.526Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"a47cc1fd-1687-4b5f-b1c8-b2b9431de4b2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_4m7of91fehx9jffwceffwymf","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/repo.rs","content":"//! File-backed repository: owns the block device, the file header and the\n//! collection of pages, and defines the persistence/sync boundary.\n//!\n//! # File layout\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! block 0              file header (one full block; CRC over [0, bs-4))\n//! block pid + 1        page `pid` (see [`crate::page`] for its layout)\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Header (little-endian):\n//! - `u32` magic `FILE_MAGIC` (`\"PFAB\"`)\n//! - `u32` format version (`FORMAT_VERSION`)\n//! - `u32` block size\n//! - `u32` page count\n//! - `u64` cumulative number of record allocations (monotonic counter)\n//! - zero padding …\n//! - `u32` CRC-32 over `[0, bs-4)`\n//!\n//! # Persistence / sync boundary\n//!\n//! Every mutating repository operation (`put`, `set`, `free`,\n//! `compact_page`, page creation) ends with:\n//!\n//! 1. exactly one whole-page [`Storage::write_block`] (fixed offset, whole\n//!    block, checksummed) — or one header write when a page is added;\n//! 2. one [`Storage::sync`] (`fsync`) when the repository was opened in\n//!    *durable* mode (the default).\n//!\n//! No operation writes two pages, so the single page write is the crash\n//! atomicity unit. Reopening after a torn write surfaces the CRC mismatch as\n//! the header write happens first, so a\n    /// crash in between simply leaves a still-unreferenced fresh page behind,\n    /// and on reopen the page is re-read and validated even if it was torn).\n    pub fn put(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Handle> {\n        if data.is_empty() {\n            return Err(Error::BadRequest(\"zero-length records are not allowed\".into()));\n        }\n        if data.len() > u16::MAX as usize {\n            return Err(Error::RecordTooLarge {\n                len: data.len(),\n                usable: self.max_record_size(),\n            });\n        }\n        let len = data.len() as u16;\n\n        // First-fit over existing pages.\n        for pid in 0..self.pages.len() {\n            match self.pages[pid].allocate(len) {\n                Ok((slot, gen)) => {\n                    let h = Handle::new(pid as u32, slot, gen);\n                    self.pages[pid].write(slot, gen, data)?;\n                    self.alloc_counter += 1;\n                    self.persist_page(pid as u32)?;\n                    return Ok(h);\n                }\n                Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) => continue,\n                Err(e) => return Err(e),\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Need a fresh page.\n        self.append_page()?;\n        let pid = self.pages.len() - 1;\n        let (slot, gen) = self.pages[pid]\n            .allocate(len)\n            .map_err(|e| match e {\n                Error::OutOfSpace { .. } => Error::RecordTooLarge {\n                    len: data.len(),\n                    usable: self.max_record_size(),\n                },\n                other => other,\n            })?;\n        self.pages[pid].write(slot, gen, data)?;\n        self.alloc_counter += 1;\n        self.persist_page(pid as u32)?;\n        Ok(Handle::new(pid as u32, slot, gen))\n    }\n\n    /// Read the record named by `h`; {"parentUuid":"a9b39585-5322-4e84-a26e-666eefed8d8f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_ej4lqh18ga50wqa0jksbp2dw","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/reference.rs","content":"//! Interval reference model.\n//!\n//! The allocator's own free-space bookkeeping (`Page::free`) is one\n//! implementation; this module is an independent model written straight from\n//! the specification: a page's data region is a set of byte intervals, each\n//! either **live** (labelled by slot + generation + payload) or **free**.\n//! Every operation is expressed as interval add/remove, and the model checks\n//! after every step that:\n//!\n//! 1. **No overlap:** no two live intervals intersect; free intervals never\n//!    intersect each other or a live interval.\n//! 2. **Space conservation:** live bytes + free bytes == data-region size at\n//!    all times; allocating n bytes moves exactly n bytes free→live; freeing\n//!    moves exactly n bytes live→free; compaction moves bytes but changes\n//!    neither count.\n//! 3. **Handle semantics:** every live handle reads back the exact payload it\n//!    was last written with; every freed or superseded generation is rejected.\n//!\n//! Tests generate random operation streams, apply each one to both the real\n//! [`Repository`](crate::repo::Repository) and this model, and compare\n//! results.\n\nuse crate::err::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::handle::Handle;\nuse crate::page::PartitionPiece;\n\n/// Model-side state of one page: data-region size and labelled live intervals.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ModelPage {\n    pub data_start: u32,\n    pub data_end: u32,\n    /// Live intervals: (start, end, slot, gen, payload).\n    pub live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32, Vec<u8>)>,\n}\n\nimpl ModelPage {\n    pub fn new(data_start: u32, data_end: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            data_start,\n            data_end,\n            live: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Total data-region capacity.\n    pub fn capacity(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.data_end - self.data_start\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of live bytes.\n    pub fn live_bytes(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| e - s).sum()\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of free bytes.\n    pub fn free_bytes(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.capacity() - self.live_bytes()\n    }\n\n    /// Largest contiguous free interval (0 if none).\n    pub fn largest_free(&self) -> u32 {\n        let mut pieces: Vec<(u32, u32)> = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| (*s, *e))\n            .collect();\n        pieces.sort_unstable();\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        let mut best = 0;\n        for (s, e) in pieces {\n            best = best.max(s - cursor);\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        best.max(self.data_end - cursor)\n    }\n\n    /// Cross-check a snapshot produced by the real allocator against the\n    /// model's own state.\n    pub fn check_snapshot(&self, snap: &[PartitionPiece]) -> Result<()> {\n        // 1. The snapshot pieces themselves must partition [data_start, data_end).\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        let mut snap_live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32)> = Vec::new();\n        for p in snap {\n            let (s, e) = match p {\n                PartitionPiece::Free { start, end } => (*start, *end),\n                PartitionPiece::Live {\n                    start,\n                    end,\n                    slot,\n                    gen,\n                } => {\n                    snap_live.push((*start, *end, *slot, *gen));\n                    (*start, *end)\n                }\n            };\n            if s != cursor {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"snapshot gap/overlap: cursor {cursor}, piece [{s},{e})\"\n                )));\n            }\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        if cursor != self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"snapshot ends at {cursor}, expected {}\",\n                self.data_end\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // 2. Live labels and sizes must match the model one-for-one.\n        let mut model_live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32)> = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(s, e, slot, gen, _)| (*s, *e, *slot, *gen))\n            .collect();\n        let key = |v: &(u32, u32, usize, u32)| (v.2, v.3);\n        snap_live.sort_by_key(key);\n        model_live.sort_by_key(key);\n        if snap_live.len() != model_live.len() {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"live record count: allocator {} vs model {}\",\n                snap_live.len(),\n                model_live.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        for (a, m) in snap_live.iter().zip(model_live.iter()) {\n            if a.2 != m.2 || a.3 != m.3 {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"live label mismatch: allocator {a:?} vs model {m:?}\"\n                )));\n            }\n            if a.1 - a.0 != m.1 - m.0 {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"record size mismatch for slot {} gen {}\",\n                    a.2, a.3\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 3. Conservation.\n        let snap_live_bytes: u32 = snap_live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _)| e - s).sum();\n        if snap_live_bytes != self.live_bytes() {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"live bytes: allocator {snap_live_bytes} vs model {}\",\n                self.live_bytes()\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Record a successful allocation in the model. Offsets are taken from\n    /// the allocator (the model does not dictate placement, only partition\n    /// validity).\n    pub fn note_allocated(\n        &mut self,\n        slot: usize,\n        gen: u32,\n        start: u32,\n        data: &[u8],\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let end = start + data.len() as u32;\n        if start < self.data_start || end > self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"allocation [{start},{end}) outside data region\"\n            )));\n        }\n        for (s, e, _, _, _) in &self.live {\n            if start < *e && *s < end {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"allocation [{start},{end}) overlaps live [{s},{e})\"\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n        self.live.push((start, end, slot, gen, data.to_vec()));\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Record a free.\n    pub fn note_freed(&mut self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> Result<()> {\n        let pos = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .position(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == slot && *g == gen)\n            .ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Model(format!(\"free of unknown slot {slot} gen {gen}\"))\n            })?;\n        self.live.swap_remove(pos);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// After compaction, refresh offsets from the allocator snapshot but keep\n    /// payloads keyed by (slot, gen).\n    pub fn note_compacted(&mut self, snap: &[PartitionPiece]) -> Result<()> {\n        for piece in snap {\n            if let PartitionPiece::Live {\n                start,\n                end,\n                slot,\n                gen,\n            } = piece\n            {\n                let entry = self\n                    .live\n                    .iter_mut()\n                    .find(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == *slot && *g == *gen)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| {\n                        Error::Model(format!(\n                            \"compaction introduced unknown live slot {slot} gen {gen}\"\n                        ))\n                    })?;\n                if end - start != entry.1 - entry.0 {\n                    return Err(Error::Model(\n                        \"compaction changed a record's length\".into(),\n                    ));\n                }\n                entry.0 = *start;\n                entry.1 = *end;\n            }\n        }\n        // Re-validate the partition with the refreshed offsets.\n        let before = self.live_bytes();\n        let mut intervals: Vec<(u32, u32)> =\n            self.live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| (*s, *e)).collect();\n        intervals.sort_unstable();\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        for (s, e) in intervals {\n            if s < cursor {\n                return Err(Error::Model(\"overlap after compaction\".into()));\n            }\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        if cursor > self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(\"live bytes exceed region after compaction\".into()));\n        }\n        if self.live_bytes() != before {\n            return Err(Error::Model(\"compaction changed live byte count\".into()));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read the model's view of a handle.\n    pub fn read(&self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.live\n            .iter()\n            .find(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == slot && *g == gen)\n            .map(|(_, _, _, _, d)| d.as_slice())\n    }\n\n    /// Model-side handle liveness check.\n    pub fn is_live(&self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> bool {\n        self.read(slot, gen).is_some()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whole-store model: one [`ModelPage`] per page.\npub struct Model {\n    pub pages: Vec<ModelPage>,\n    /// (slot, gen) payload expectations are kept per page; also track the\n    /// latest generation ever issued per slot to assert old handles fail.\n}\n\nimpl Model {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self { pages: Vec::new() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn page(&self, pid: u32) -> Option<&ModelPage> {\n        self.pages.get(pid as usize)\n    }\n\n    pub fn page_mut(&mut self, pid: u32) -> Option<&mut ModelPage> {\n        self.pages.get_mut(pid as usize)\n    }\n\n    pub fn ensure_page(&mut self, pid: u32, data_start: u32, data_end: u32) {\n        while self.pages.len() <= pid as usize {\n            self.pages.push(ModelPage::new(data_start, data_end));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Store-wide conservation: sum(page capacities) == live + free.\n    pub fn check_conservation(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        for p in &self.pages {\n            if p.live_bytes() + p.free_bytes() != p.capacity() {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"space not conserved: cap {} live {} free {}\",\n                    p.capacity(),\n                    p.live_bytes(),\n                    p.free_bytes()\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Assert a handle must be dead in the model.\n    pub fn assert_dead(&self, h: Handle) -> Result<()> {\n        match self.page(h.page) {\n            Some(p) if p.is_live(h.slot_index(), h.gen) => Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"handle {h} expected dead but model has it live\"\n            ))),\n            _ => Ok(()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for Model {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn free_calc_fragments() {\n        let mut p = ModelPage::new(0, 100);\n        p.note_allocated(0, 1, 10, &[0; 10]).unwrap();\n        p.note_allocated(1, 1, 30, &[0; 5]).unwrap();\n        // free: [0,10)=10 [20,30)=10 [35,100)=65 -> largest 65\n        assert_eq!(p.live_bytes(), 15);\n        assert_eq!(p.free_bytes(), 85);\n        assert_eq!(p.largest_free(), 65);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn overlap_rejected() {\n        let mut p = ModelPage::new(0, 100);\n        p.note_allocated(0, 1, 10, &[0; 10]).unwrap();\n        assert!(p.note_allocated(1, 1, 15, &[0; 5]).is_err());\n Interval reference model.\n//!\n//! The allocator's own free-space bookkeeping (`Page::free`) is one\n//! implementation; this module is an independent model written straight from\n//! the specification: a page's data region is a set of byte intervals, each\n//! either **live** (labelled by slot + generation + payload) or **free**.\n//! Every operation is expressed as interval add/remove, and the model checks\n//! after every step that:\n//!\n//! 1. **No overlap:** no two live intervals intersect; free intervals never\n//!    intersect each other or a live interval.\n//! 2. **Space conservation:** live bytes + free bytes == data-region size at\n//!    all times; allocating n bytes moves exactly n bytes free→live; freeing\n//!    moves exactly n bytes live→free; compaction moves bytes but changes\n//!    neither count.\n//! 3. **Handle semantics:** every live handle reads back the exact payload it\n//!    was last written with; every freed or superseded generation is rejected.\n//!\n//! Tests generate random operation streams, apply each one to both the real\n//! [`Repository`](crate::repo::Repository) and this model, and compare\n//! results.\n\nuse crate::err::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::handle::Handle;\nuse crate::page::PartitionPiece;\n\n/// Model-side state of one page: data-region size and labelled live intervals.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ModelPage {\n    pub data_start: u32,\n    pub data_end: u32,\n    /// Live intervals: (start, end, slot, gen, payload).\n    pub live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32, Vec<u8>)>,\n}\n\nimpl ModelPage {\n    pub fn new(data_start: u32, data_end: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            data_start,\n            data_end,\n            live: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Total data-region capacity.\n    pub fn capacity(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.data_end - self.data_start\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of live bytes.\n    pub fn live_bytes(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| e - s).sum()\n    }\n\n    /// Sum of free bytes.\n    pub fn free_bytes(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.capacity() - self.live_bytes()\n    }\n\n    /// Largest contiguous free interval (0 if none).\n    pub fn largest_free(&self) -> u32 {\n        let mut pieces: Vec<(u32, u32)> = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| (*s, *e))\n            .collect();\n        pieces.sort_unstable();\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        let mut best = 0;\n        for (s, e) in pieces {\n            best = best.max(s - cursor);\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        best.max(self.data_end - cursor)\n    }\n\n    /// Cross-check a snapshot produced by the real allocator against the\n    /// model's own state.\n    pub fn check_snapshot(&self, snap: &[PartitionPiece]) -> Result<()> {\n        // 1. The snapshot pieces themselves must partition [data_start, data_end).\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        let mut snap_live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32)> = Vec::new();\n        for p in snap {\n            let (s, e) = match p {\n                PartitionPiece::Free { start, end } => (*start, *end),\n                PartitionPiece::Live {\n                    start,\n                    end,\n                    slot,\n                    gen,\n                } => {\n                    snap_live.push((*start, *end, *slot, *gen));\n                    (*start, *end)\n                }\n            };\n            if s != cursor {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"snapshot gap/overlap: cursor {cursor}, piece [{s},{e})\"\n                )));\n            }\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        if cursor != self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"snapshot ends at {cursor}, expected {}\",\n                self.data_end\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // 2. Live labels and sizes must match the model one-for-one.\n        let mut model_live: Vec<(u32, u32, usize, u32)> = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(s, e, slot, gen, _)| (*s, *e, *slot, *gen))\n            .collect();\n        let key = |v: &(u32, u32, usize, u32)| (v.2, v.3);\n        snap_live.sort_by_key(key);\n        model_live.sort_by_key(key);\n        if snap_live.len() != model_live.len() {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"live record count: allocator {} vs model {}\",\n                snap_live.len(),\n                model_live.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        for (a, m) in snap_live.iter().zip(model_live.iter()) {\n            if a.2 != m.2 || a.3 != m.3 {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"live label mismatch: allocator {a:?} vs model {m:?}\"\n                )));\n            }\n            if a.1 - a.0 != m.1 - m.0 {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"record size mismatch for slot {} gen {}\",\n                    a.2, a.3\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n\n        // 3. Conservation.\n        let snap_live_bytes: u32 = snap_live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _)| e - s).sum();\n        if snap_live_bytes != self.live_bytes() {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"live bytes: allocator {snap_live_bytes} vs model {}\",\n                self.live_bytes()\n            )));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Record a successful allocation in the model. Offsets are taken from\n    /// the allocator (the model does not dictate placement, only partition\n    /// validity).\n    pub fn note_allocated(\n        &mut self,\n        slot: usize,\n        gen: u32,\n        start: u32,\n        data: &[u8],\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        let end = start + data.len() as u32;\n        if start < self.data_start || end > self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"allocation [{start},{end}) outside data region\"\n            )));\n        }\n        for (s, e, _, _, _) in &self.live {\n            if start < *e && *s < end {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"allocation [{start},{end}) overlaps live [{s},{e})\"\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n        self.live.push((start, end, slot, gen, data.to_vec()));\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Record a free.\n    pub fn note_freed(&mut self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> Result<()> {\n        let pos = self\n            .live\n            .iter()\n            .position(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == slot && *g == gen)\n            .ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Model(format!(\"free of unknown slot {slot} gen {gen}\"))\n            })?;\n        self.live.swap_remove(pos);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// After compaction, refresh offsets from the allocator snapshot but keep\n    /// payloads keyed by (slot, gen).\n    pub fn note_compacted(&mut self, snap: &[PartitionPiece]) -> Result<()> {\n        for piece in snap {\n            if let PartitionPiece::Live {\n                start,\n                end,\n                slot,\n                gen,\n            } = piece\n            {\n                let entry = self\n                    .live\n                    .iter_mut()\n                    .find(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == *slot && *g == *gen)\n                    .ok_or_else(|| {\n                        Error::Model(format!(\n                            \"compaction introduced unknown live slot {slot} gen {gen}\"\n                        ))\n                    })?;\n                if end - start != entry.1 - entry.0 {\n                    return Err(Error::Model(\n                        \"compaction changed a record's length\".into(),\n                    ));\n                }\n                entry.0 = *start;\n                entry.1 = *end;\n            }\n        }\n        // Re-validate the partition with the refreshed offsets.\n        let before = self.live_bytes();\n        let mut intervals: Vec<(u32, u32)> =\n            self.live.iter().map(|(s, e, _, _, _)| (*s, *e)).collect();\n        intervals.sort_unstable();\n        let mut cursor = self.data_start;\n        for (s, e) in intervals {\n            if s < cursor {\n                return Err(Error::Model(\"overlap after compaction\".into()));\n            }\n            cursor = e;\n        }\n        if cursor > self.data_end {\n            return Err(Error::Model(\"live bytes exceed region after compaction\".into()));\n        }\n        if self.live_bytes() != before {\n            return Err(Error::Model(\"compaction changed live byte count\".into()));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read the model's view of a handle.\n    pub fn read(&self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        self.live\n            .iter()\n            .find(|(_, _, s, g, _)| *s == slot && *g == gen)\n            .map(|(_, _, _, _, d)| d.as_slice())\n    }\n\n    /// Model-side handle liveness check.\n    pub fn is_live(&self, slot: usize, gen: u32) -> bool {\n        self.read(slot, gen).is_some()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whole-store model: one [`ModelPage`] per page.\npub struct Model {\n    pub pages: Vec<ModelPage>,\n    /// (slot, gen) payload expectations are kept per page; also track the\n    /// latest generation ever issued per slot to assert old handles fail.\n}\n\nimpl Model {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self { pages: Vec::new() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn page(&self, pid: u32) -> Option<&ModelPage> {\n        self.pages.get(pid as usize)\n    }\n\n    pub fn page_mut(&mut self, pid: u32) -> Option<&mut ModelPage> {\n        self.pages.get_mut(pid as usize)\n    }\n\n    pub fn ensure_page(&mut self, pid: u32, data_start: u32, data_end: u32) {\n        while self.pages.len() <= pid as usize {\n            self.pages.push(ModelPage::new(data_start, data_end));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Store-wide conservation: sum(page capacities) == live + free.\n    pub fn check_conservation(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        for p in &self.pages {\n            if p.live_bytes() + p.free_bytes() != p.capacity() {\n                return Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                    \"space not conserved: cap {} live {} free {}\",\n                    p.capacity(),\n                    p.live_bytes(),\n                    p.free_bytes()\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Assert a handle must be dead in the model.\n    pub fn assert_dead(&self, h: Handle) -> Result<()> {\n        match self.page(h.page) {\n            Some(p) if p.is_live(h.slot_index(), h.gen) => Err(Error::Model(format!(\n                \"handle {h} expected dead but model has it live\"\n            ))),\n            _ => Ok(()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for Model {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn free_calc_fragments() {\n        let mut p = ModelPage::new(0, 100);\n        p.note_allocated(0, 1, 10, &[0; 10]).unwrap();\n        p.note_allocated(1, 1, 30, &[0; 5]).unwrap();\n        // free: [0,10)=10 [20,30)=10 [35,100)=65 -> largest 65\n        assert_eq!(p.live_bytes(), 15);\n        assert_eq!(p.free_bytes(), 85);\n        assert_eq!(p.largest_free(), 65);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn overlap_rejected() {\n        let mut p = ModelPage::new(0, 100);\n        p.note_allocated(0, 1, 10, &[0; 10]).unwrap();\n        assert!(p.note_allocated(1, 1, 15, &[0; 5]).is_err());\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"79cb06f7-def4-4516-9aa5-080df0a04608","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"fe8097e5-c7e1-41b8-9b20-b826269b4ff5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_v3d2mqlevhifpakflwz8tb0p","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/lib.rs","content":"//! # pfa — page-level free-space allocator\n//!\n//! A pure-backend, file-backed store for variable-length records:\n//!\n//! - [`page`] implements the slotted page with an explicit free-space region\n//!   (interval split on allocation, merge on free), per-slot generations and\n//!   in-place compaction that preserves live handle semantics.\n//! - [`repo`] implements the file-backed repository with a checksummed header,\n//!   one page per fixed-size block, and a clearly defined sync boundary\n//!   (one whole-page write + optional `fsync` per mutation).\n//! - [`io`] is the injectable I/O layer: real files, in-memory images and a\n//!   fault-injecting decorator used to simulate disk errors and torn writes.\n//! - [`reference`] is an independent interval reference model used by the\n//!   test-suite to prove no-overlap and space-conservation invariants.\n//! - [`http`] exposes a small local HTTP validation endpoint.\n\npub mod crc;\npub mod err;\npub mod handle;\npub mod io;\npub mod page;\npub mod reference;\npub mod repo;\n\n#[cfg(feature = \"http\")]\npub mod http;\n\npub use err::{Error, Result};\npub use handle::Handle;\npub use io::{Fault, FaultKind, FaultOp, FaultPolicy, FaultyStorage, FileStorage, MemStorage, Storage};\npub use page::{Page, PartitionPiece};\npub use reference::{Model, ModelPage};\npub use repo::{Repository, Stats};\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_9d6aa89c07ddbf9463adbbc7","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":5726,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":52024,"output_tokens":698,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"37d62a13-476f-4788-8273-0db9fcbfbc07","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:11:11.527Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}
