{"parentUuid":"c19f584f-2a3f-4b0a-b28e-a4379def03ea","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_wq1wccxe018npp7i33eiznqn","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/src/http.rs","content":"//! Local HTTP validation endpoint (pure `std`, no third-party dependencies).\n//!\n//! This is *not* a production server — it is a deliberately small, local\n//! harness so the allocator can be exercised end-to-end over HTTP with\n//! `curl`. Record payloads are carried as hexadecimal strings, which keeps the\n//! JSON framing trivial and lets arbitrary bytes round-trip.\n//!\n//! ## Routes\n//!\n//! | Method | Path                     | Body / query                                  |\n//! |--------|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|\n//! | GET    | `/health`                | —                                             |\n//! | POST   | `/records`               | `{\"data_hex\":\"…\"}` or `{\"data\":\"utf-8 text\"}` |\n//! | GET    | `/records?handle=…`      | —                                             |\n//! | PUT    | `/records`               | `{\"handle\":\"p0.s1.g2\",\"data_hex\":\"…\"}`        |\n//! | DELETE | `/records?handle=…`      | —                                             |\n//! | POST   | `/compact`               | `{}` or `{\"page\":0}`                          |\n//! | GET    | `/stats`                 | —                                             |\n//! | GET    | `/partitions`            | interval reference-model snapshot             |\n//! | POST   | `/reopen`                | close & reopen the file (re-checksum all)     |\n\nuse crate::err::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::io::FileStorage;\nuse crate::repo::Repository;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nstruct AppState {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    repo: Option<Repository<FileStorage>>,\n}\n\n/// Run the HTTP server until the process is killed.\npub fn serve(path: PathBuf, block_size: u32, addr: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let create = !path.exists() || std::fs::metadata(&path)?.len() == 0;\n    let storage = FileStorage::open(&path, block_size)?;\n    let repo = if create {\n        Repository::create(storage, block_size)?\n    } else {\n        Repository::open(storage, block_size)?\n    };\n    let state = Mutex::new(AppState {\n        path,\n        block_size,\n        repo: Some(repo),\n    });\n\n    let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n    eprintln!(\"pfa listening on http://{addr} (block_size={block_size})\");\n    for stream in listener.incoming() {\n        match stream {\n            Ok(stream) => {\n                stream.set_nodelay(true).ok();\n                stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(10))).ok();\n                if let Err(e) = handle_connection(stream, &state) {\n                    eprintln!(\"connection error: {e}\");\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => eprintln!(\"accept error: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(mut stream: TcpStream, state: &Mutex<AppState>) -> Result<()> {\n    let mut req_buf = [0u8; 64 * 1024];\n    let mut total = 0usize;\n    // Read headers.\n    let header_end = loop {\n        if total == req_buf.len() {\n            write_simple(&mut stream, 413, \"request too large\", b\"{}\")?;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let n = stream.read(&mut req_buf[total..])?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        total += n;\n        if let Some(pos) = find_subseq(&req_buf[..total], b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") {\n            break pos + 4;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&req_buf[..header_end]).to_string();\n    let mut lines = head.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"/\").to_string();\n    let (path, query) = match target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (target.clone(), String::new()),\n    };\n\n    let mut content_length = 0usize;\n    for line in lines {\n        if let Some(rest) = line\n            .split_once(':')\n            .map(|(k, v)| (k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim()))\n        {\n            if rest.0 == \"content-length\" {\n                content_length = rest.1.parse().unwrap_or(0);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Read any remaining body bytes.\n    let mut body = req_buf[header_end..total].to_vec();\n    while body.len() < content_length {\n        let mut chunk = vec![0u8; content_length - body.len()];\n        let n = stream.read(&mut chunk)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        body.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);\n    }\n    body.truncate(content_length);\n\n    let response = route(state, &method, &path, &query, &body);\n    let (status, reason, payload) = match response {\n        Ok(json) => (200, \"OK\", json),\n        Err(e) => error_response(&e),\n    };\n    write_simple(&mut stream, status, reason, payload.as_bytes())?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn error_response(e: &Error) -> (u16, &'static str, String) {\n    let (status, reason, code) = match e {\n        Error::BadRequest(_) => (400, \"Bad Request\", \"bad_request\"),\n        Error::NoSuchSlot { .. } => (404, \"Not Found\", \"no_such_slot\"),\n        Error::StaleHandle { .. } => (409, \"Conflict\", \"stale_handle\"),\n        Error::RecordTooLarge { .. } => (413, \"Payload Too Large\", \"record_too_large\"),\n        Error::OutOfSpace { .. } => (422, \"Unprocessable Entity\", \"out_of_space\"),\n        Error::LengthMismatch { .. } => (422, \"Unprocessable Entity\", \"length_mismatch\"),\n        Error::Corrupt(_) => (500, \"Internal Server Error\", \"corrupt\"),\n        Error::Io(_) | Error::BadConfig(_) | Error::Model(_) => {\n            (500, \"Internal Server Error\", \"internal\")\n        }\n    };\n    let body = json::object(vec![\n        (\"error\", json::string(code)),\n        (\"message\", json::string(&e.to_string())),\n    ]);\n    (status, reason, body)\n}\n\nfn route(\n    state: &Mutex<AppState>,\n    method: &str,\n    path: &str,\n    query: &str,\n    body: &[u8],\n) -> Result<String> {\n    match (method, path) {\n        (\"GET\", \"/\") | (\"GET\", \"/health\") => Ok(json::object(vec![\n            (\"status\", json::string(\"ok\")),\n            (\"service\", json::string(\"pfa\")),\n        ])),\n\n        (\"POST\", \"/records\") => {\n            let data = parse_payload(body)?;\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_mut().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            let h = repo.put(&data)?;\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"handle\", json::string(&h.to_string())),\n                (\"bytes\", json::uint(data.len() as u64)),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"GET\", \"/records\") => {\n            let h = parse_handle_query(query)?;\n            let st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            let data = repo.get(h)?;\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"handle\", json::string(&h.to_string())),\n                (\"data_hex\", json::string(&hex::encode(&data))),\n                (\"bytes\", json::uint(data.len() as u64)),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"PUT\", \"/records\") => {\n            let obj = json::parse_flat(body)?;\n            let h = obj\n                .get(\"handle\")\n                .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"missing handle\".into()))?\n                .parse()?;\n            let data = parse_payload(body)?;\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_mut().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            repo.set(h, &data)?;\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"handle\", json::string(&h.to_string())),\n                (\"updated\", json::BOOL_TRUE),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"DELETE\", \"/records\") => {\n            let h = parse_handle_query(query)?;\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_mut().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            repo.free(h)?;\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"handle\", json::string(&h.to_string())),\n                (\"freed\", json::BOOL_TRUE),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"POST\", \"/free\") => {\n            // Alias for DELETE /records with the handle in the JSON body.\n            let obj = json::parse_flat(body)?;\n            let h: crate::handle::Handle = obj\n                .get(\"handle\")\n                .ok_or_else(|| Error::BadRequest(\"missing handle\".into()))?\n                .parse()?;\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_mut().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            repo.free(h)?;\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"handle\", json::string(&h.to_string())),\n                (\"freed\", json::BOOL_TRUE),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"POST\", \"/compact\") => {\n            let page = if body.is_empty() || body.trim_ascii().is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                let obj = json::parse_flat(body)?;\n                obj.get(\"page\").map(|s| s.parse::<u32>()).transpose().map_err(\n                    |_| Error::BadRequest(\"page must be a non-negative integer\".into()),\n                )?\n            };\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_mut().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            let relocated = match page {\n                Some(pid) => repo.compact_page(pid)?,\n                None => repo.compact_all()?,\n            };\n            Ok(json::object(vec![\n                (\"compacted\", json::BOOL_TRUE),\n                (\"relocated_bytes\", json::uint(relocated as u64)),\n            ]))\n        }\n\n        (\"GET\", \"/stats\") => {\n            let st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            Ok(stats_json(repo.stats()))\n        }\n\n        (\"GET\", \"/partitions\") => {\n            let st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let repo = st.repo.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository is closed (reopen failed previously)\".into())\n            })?;\n            let pages: Vec<String> = repo\n                .partition_snapshot()\n                .iter()\n                .enumerate()\n                .map(|(pid, pieces)| {\n                    let items: Vec<String> = pieces\n                        .iter()\n                        .map(|p| match p {\n                            crate::page::PartitionPiece::Free { start, end } => json::object(\n                                vec![\n                                    (\"kind\", json::string(\"free\")),\n                                    (\"start\", json::uint(*start as u64)),\n                                    (\"end\", json::uint(*end as u64)),\n                                    (\"bytes\", json::uint((end - start) as u64)),\n                                ],\n                            ),\n                            crate::page::PartitionPiece::Live {\n                                start,\n                                end,\n                                slot,\n                                gen,\n                            } => json::object(vec![\n                                (\"kind\", json::string(\"live\")),\n                                (\"start\", json::uint(*start as u64)),\n                                (\"end\", json::uint(*end as u64)),\n                                (\"bytes\", json::uint((end - start) as u64)),\n                                (\"slot\", json::uint(*slot as u64)),\n                                (\"gen\", json::uint(*gen as u64)),\n                            ]),\n                        })\n                        .collect();\n                    json::object(vec![\n                        (\"page\", json::uint(pid as u64)),\n                        (\"pieces\", json::array(items)),\n                    ])\n                })\n                .collect();\n            Ok(json::object(vec![(\"pages\", json::array(pages))]))\n        }\n\n        (\"POST\", \"/reopen\") => {\n            let mut st = state.lock().expect(\"state mutex poisoned\");\n            let taken = st.repo.take().ok_or_else(|| {\n                Error::Corrupt(\"repository already closed\".into())\n            })?;\n            let (path, block_size) = (st.path.clone(), st.block_size);\n            let reopened = match taken\n                .into_storage()\n                // FileStorage owns the file handle; drop it, then re-open.\n                .reopen_via_path(&path, block_size)\n            {\n                Ok(r) => r,\n                Err(e) => return Err(e),\n            };\n }\n}\n\nfn parse_handle_query(query: &str) -> Result<crate::handle::Handle> {\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        if let Some(v) = pair.strip_prefix(\"handle=\") {\n            let decoded = Commands:\n//! - `pfa serve [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080] [--block-size 4096] [--file pfa.db]`\n//!   run the local HTTP validation endpoint.\n//! - `pfa check --file pfa.db [--block-size 4096]`\n//!   open the file, validate the header and every page CRC/partition and\n//!   print statistics.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\n\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::io::FileStorage;\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nstruct Args {\n    addr: String,\n    file: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    durable: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Args {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            addr: \"127.0.0.1:8080\".to_string(),\n            file: PathBuf::from(\"pfa.db\"),\n            block_size: 4096,\n            durable: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn parse_args(argv: &[String]) -> Result<(String, Args), String> {\n    let mut args = Args::default();\n    let mut iter = argv.iter();\n    let cmd = iter.next().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| \"serve\".to_string());\n    while let Some(a) = iter.next() {\n        match a.as_str() {\n            \"--addr\" => {\n                args.addr = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--addr needs a value\")?\n                    .clone();\n            }\n            \"--file\" => {\n                args.file = PathBuf::from(iter.next().ok_or(\"--file needs a value\")?);\n            }\n            \"--block-size\" => {\n                args.block_size = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--block-size needs a value\")?\n                    .parse()\n                    .map_err(|_| \"block-size must be a positive integer\")?;\n            }\n            \"--no-sync\" => args.durable = false,\n            other => return Err(format!(\"unknown argument {other}\")),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok((cmd, args))\n}\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();\n    let (cmd, args) = match parse_args(&argv) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"usage: pfa [serve|check] [--addr ADDR] [--file PATH] [--block-size N]\");\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n\n    match cmd.as_str() {\n        \"serve\" => match pfa::http::serve(args.file.clone(), args.block_size, &args.addr) {\n            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n            Err(Error::Io(e)) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AddrInUse => {\n                eprintln!(\"bind failed: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::from(1)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!(\"server error: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::FAILURE\n            }\n        },\n        \"check\" => run_check(&args),\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command {other:?} (expected serve or check)\");\n            ExitCode::from(2)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run_check(args: &Args) -> ExitCode {\n    let storage = match FileStorage::open(&args.file, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"cannot open {}: {e}\", args.file.display());\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    match Repository::open(storage, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(repo) => {\n            let s = repo.stats();\n            println!(\n                \"OK  file={} block_size={} pages={} alloc_counter={}\",\n                args.file.display(),\n                s.block_size,\n                s.page_count,\n                s.alloc_counter\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"    live_records={} live_bytes={} free_bytes={} free_intervals={}\",\n                s.live_records, s.live_bytes, s.free_bytes, s.free_intervals\n            );\n            for p in &s.pages {\n                println!(\n                    \"    page {}: live={} ({} bytes), free={} bytes in {} intervals\",\n                    p.pid, p.live_records, Commands:\n//! - `pfa serve [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080] [--block-size 4096] [--file pfa.db]`\n//!   run the local HTTP validation endpoint.\n//! - `pfa check --file pfa.db [--block-size 4096]`\n//!   open the file, validate the header and every page CRC/partition and\n//!   print statistics.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\n\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::io::FileStorage;\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nstruct Args {\n    addr: String,\n    file: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    durable: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Args {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            addr: \"127.0.0.1:8080\".to_string(),\n            file: PathBuf::from(\"pfa.db\"),\n            block_size: 4096,\n            durable: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn parse_args(argv: &[String]) -> Result<(String, Args), String> {\n    let mut args = Args::default();\n    let mut iter = argv.iter();\n    let cmd = iter.next().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| \"serve\".to_string());\n    while let Some(a) = iter.next() {\n        match a.as_str() {\n            \"--addr\" => {\n                args.addr = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--addr needs a value\")?\n                    .clone();\n            }\n            \"--file\" => {\n                args.file = PathBuf::from(iter.next().ok_or(\"--file needs a value\")?);\n            }\n            \"--block-size\" => {\n                args.block_size = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--block-size needs a value\")?\n                    .parse()\n                    .map_err(|_| \"block-size must be a positive integer\")?;\n            }\n            \"--no-sync\" => args.durable = false,\n            other => return Err(format!(\"unknown argument {other}\")),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok((cmd, args))\n}\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();\n    let (cmd, args) = match parse_args(&argv) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"usage: pfa [serve|check] [--addr ADDR] [--file PATH] [--block-size N]\");\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n\n    match cmd.as_str() {\n        \"serve\" => match pfa::http::serve(args.file.clone(), args.block_size, &args.addr) {\n            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n            Err(Error::Io(e)) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AddrInUse => {\n                eprintln!(\"bind failed: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::from(1)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!(\"server error: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::FAILURE\n            }\n        },\n        \"check\" => run_check(&args),\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command {other:?} (expected serve or check)\");\n            ExitCode::from(2)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run_check(args: &Args) -> ExitCode {\n    let storage = match FileStorage::open(&args.file, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"cannot open {}: {e}\", args.file.display());\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    match Repository::open(storage, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(repo) => {\n            let s = repo.stats();\n            println!(\n                \"OK  file={} block_size={} pages={} alloc_counter={}\",\n                args.file.display(),\n                s.block_size,\n                s.page_count,\n                s.alloc_counter\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"    live_records={} live_bytes={} free_bytes={} free_intervals={}\",\n                s.live_records, s.live_bytes, s.free_bytes, s.free_intervals\n            );\n            for p in &s.pages {\n                println!(\n                    \"    page {}: live={} ({} bytes), free={} bytes in {} intervals\",\n                    p.pid, p.live_records, p.live_bytes, p.free_bytes, p.free_intervals\n                );\n            }\n            let _ = args.durable;\n            ExitCode::SUCCESS\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"CHECK FAILED: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"eab1a446-31e4-407e-a726-f706c8c1814e","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

the file, validate the header and every page CRC/partition and\n//!   print statistics.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\n\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::io::FileStorage;\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nstruct Args {\n    addr: String,\n    file: PathBuf,\n    block_size: u32,\n    durable: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Args {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            addr: \"127.0.0.1:8080\".to_string(),\n            file: PathBuf::from(\"pfa.db\"),\n            block_size: 4096,\n            durable: true,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn parse_args(argv: &[String]) -> Result<(String, Args), String> {\n    let mut args = Args::default();\n    let mut iter = argv.iter();\n    let cmd = iter.next().cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| \"serve\".to_string());\n    while let Some(a) = iter.next() {\n        match a.as_str() {\n            \"--addr\" => {\n                args.addr = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--addr needs a value\")?\n                    .clone();\n            }\n            \"--file\" => {\n                args.file = PathBuf::from(iter.next().ok_or(\"--file needs a value\")?);\n            }\n            \"--block-size\" => {\n                args.block_size = iter\n                    .next()\n                    .ok_or(\"--block-size needs a value\")?\n                    .parse()\n                    .map_err(|_| \"block-size must be a positive integer\")?;\n            }\n            \"--no-sync\" => args.durable = false,\n            other => return Err(format!(\"unknown argument {other}\")),\n        }\n    }\n    Ok((cmd, args))\n}\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();\n    let (cmd, args) = match parse_args(&argv) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"usage: pfa [serve|check] [--addr ADDR] [--file PATH] [--block-size N]\");\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n\n    match cmd.as_str() {\n        \"serve\" => match pfa::http::serve(args.file.clone(), args.block_size, &args.addr) {\n            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n            Err(Error::Io(e)) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AddrInUse => {\n                eprintln!(\"bind failed: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::from(1)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                eprintln!(\"server error: {e}\");\n                ExitCode::FAILURE\n            }\n        },\n        \"check\" => run_check(&args),\n        other => {\n            eprintln!(\"unknown command {other:?} (expected serve or check)\");\n            ExitCode::from(2)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn run_check(args: &Args) -> ExitCode {\n    let storage = match FileStorage::open(&args.file, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"cannot open {}: {e}\", args.file.display());\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    match Repository::open(storage, args.block_size) {\n        Ok(repo) => {\n            let s = repo.stats();\n            println!(\n                \"OK  file={} block_size={} pages={} alloc_counter={}\",\n                args.file.display(),\n                s.block_size,\n                s.page_count,\n                s.alloc_counter\n            );\n            println!(\n                \"    live_records={} live_bytes={} free_bytes={} free_intervals={}\",\n                s.live_records, s.live_bytes, s.free_bytes, s.free_intervals\n            );\n            for p in &s.pages {\n                println!(\n                    \"    page {}: live={} ({} bytes), free={} bytes in {} intervals\",\n                    p.pid, p.live_records, p.live_bytes, p.free_bytes, p.free_intervals\n                );\n            }\n            let _ = args.durable;\n            ExitCode::SUCCESS\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n Shared test helpers.\n#![allow(dead_code)]\n\nuse pfa::page::{Page, PAGE_HEADER_LEN, SLOT_LEN};\nuse pfa::reference::ModelPage;\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\nuse pfa::{PartitionPiece, Storage};\n\n/// Deterministic xorshift PRNG so randomized tests are reproducible.\npub struct Rng(u64);\n\nimpl Rng {\n    pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {\n        Rng(seed.max(1))\n    }\n    pub fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {\n        let mut x = self.0;\n        x ^= x << 13;\n        x ^= x >> 7;\n        x ^= x << 17;\n        self.0 = x;\n        x\n    }\n    pub fn below(&mut self, n: u64) -> usize {\n        (self.next_u64() % n) as usize\n    }\n    pub fn chance(&mut self, pct: u64) -> bool {\n        self.next_u64() % 100 < pct\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build a deterministic payload: `tag` byte repeated, with an 8-byte big\n/// endian nonce prefix so different allocations are distinguishable after\n/// recycling.\npub fn payload(seed: u64, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let tag = (seed as u8) ^ 0xA5;\n    let mut v = vec![tag; len];\n    v[..8.min(len)].copy_from_slice(&seed.to_be_bytes()[..8.min(len)]);\n    v\n}\n\n/// Data region boundaries for a page decoded under `block_size` with the given\n/// number of slots.\npub fn data_region(slot_count: usize, block_size: u32) -> (u32, u32) {\n    (\n        PAGE_HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN * slot_count as u32,\n        block_size - 4,\n    )\n}\n\n/// Build/refresh a [`ModelPage`] view directly from a live [`Page`] snapshot:\n/// the model takes the allocator's offsets but keeps its own expectations\n/// about sizes/labels; the harness uses this to check partition conservation.\npub fn model_from_page(page: &Page) -> ModelPage {\n    let (ds, de) = data_region(page.slot_count(), page.block_size());\n    let mut mp = ModelPage::new(ds, de);\n    for piece in page.partition_snapshot() {\n        if let PartitionPiece::Live {\n            start,\n            end,\n            slot,\n            gen,\n        } = piece\n        {\n            mp.note_allocated(slot, gen, start, &vec![0u8; (end - start) as usize])\n                .expect(\"model: page snapshot not a valid partition\");\n        }\n    }\n    mp\n}\n\n/// Verify the partition of every page of an open repository against the\n/// reference model: no overlap, exact cover, conservation.\npub fn assert_partitions<S: Storage>(repo: &Repository<S>) {\n    for pid in 0..repo.page_count() {\n        let page = repo.page(pid).expect(\"page exists\");\n        page.verify_partition().expect(\"allocator partition invariant\");\n        let mp = model_from_page(page);\n        mp.check_snapshot(&page.partition_snapshot())\n            .expect(\"reference model agrees with allocator\");\n        mp.check_conservation().expect(\"space conserved\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// Store-wide space accounting: per page, data region size == live + free.\npub fn assert_space_accounting<S: Storage>(repo: &Repository<S>) {\n    for pid in 0..repo.page_count() {\n        let page = repo.page(pid).unwrap();\n        let (ds, de) = data_region(page.slot_count(), page.block_size());\n        let live: u32 = page\n            .partition_snapshot()\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|p| match p {\n                PartitionPiece::Live { start, end, .. } => Some(end - start),\n                _ => None,\n            })\n            .sum();\n        assert_eq!(\n            live + page.free_bytes() as u32,\n            de - ds,\n            \"page {pid}: live + free != data region\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_0d93cc0b36b2d3b3bbb96cac","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1019,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":75576,"output_tokens":1126,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"81c2186b-dbc4-45e7-acc8-3a091d1bf195","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:18:40.056Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

len];\n    v[..8.min(len)].copy_from_slice(&seed.to_be_bytes()[..8.min(len)]);\n    v\n}\n\n/// Data region boundaries for a page decoded under `block_size` with the given\n/// number of slots.\npub fn data_region(slot_count: usize, block_size: u32) -> (u32, u32) {\n    (\n        PAGE_HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN * slot_count as u32,\n        block_size - 4,\n    )\n}\n\n/// Build/refresh a [`ModelPage`] view directly from a live [`Page`] snapshot:\n/// the model takes the allocator's offsets but keeps its own expectations\n/// about sizes/labels; the harness uses this to check partition conservation.\npub fn model_from_page(page: &Page) -> ModelPage {\n    let (ds, de) = data_region(page.slot_count(), page.block_size());\n    let mut mp = ModelPage::new(ds, de);\n    for piece in page.partition_snapshot() {\n        if let PartitionPiece::Live {\n            start,\n            end,\n            slot,\n            gen,\n        } = piece\n        {\n            mp.note_allocated(slot, gen, start, &vec![0u8; (end - start) as usize])\n                .expect(\"model: page snapshot not a valid partition\");\n        }\n    }\n    mp\n}\n\n/// Verify the partition of every page of an open repository against the\n/// reference model: no overlap, exact cover, conservation.\npub fn assert_partitions<S: Storage>(repo: &Repository<S>) {\n    for pid in 0..repo.page_count() {\n        let page = repo.page(pid).expect(\"page exists\");\n        page.verify_partition().expect(\"allocator partition invariant\");\n        let mp = model_from_page(page);\n        mp.check_snapshot(&page.partition_snapshot())\n            .expect(\"reference model agrees with allocator\");\n        mp.check_conservation().expect(\"space conserved\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// Store-wide space accounting: per page, data region size == live + free.\npub fn assert_space_accounting<S: Storage>(repo: &Repository<S>) {\n    for pid in 0..repo.page_count() {\n        let page = repo.page(pid).unwrap();\n        let (ds, de) = data_region(page.slot_count(), page.block_size());\n        let live: u32 = page\n            .partition_snapshot()\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|p| match p {\n                PartitionPiece::Live { start, end, .. } => Some(end - start),\n                _ => None,\n            })\n            .sum();\n        assert_eq!(\n            live + page.free_bytes() as u32,\n            de - ds,\n            \"page {pid}: live + free != data region\"\n        );\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"81c2186b-dbc4-45e7-acc8-3a091d1bf195","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"cd4a999a-bef3-4ed6-9b00-ec63d8cf46c7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_6y2futk17021839ihkqah9ht","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/tests/acceptance.rs","content":"//! Acceptance test: fragmented allocation, double-free, stale handles,\n//! compaction — driven against the interval reference model.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::handle::Handle;\nuse pfa::io::MemStorage;\nuse pfa::page::{PartitionPiece, PAGE_HEADER_LEN, SLOT_LEN};\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nconst BS: u32 = 256;\n\n/// Construct an obviously fragmented page: interleaved allocations and frees\n/// leave many small free intervals; then assert the free space is genuinely\n/// unusable in aggregate until compaction merges it.\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_allocation_blocks_until_compaction() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    // Fill a page with many small records.\n    let mut handles = Vec::new();\n    let fill_len = 12u16;\n    loop {\n        match r.put(&payload(handles.len() as u64, fill_len as usize)) {\n            Ok(h) => handles.push(h),\n            Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) | Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let slots = r.page(0).unwrap().slot_count();\n    let intervals_before = r.page(0).unwrap().free_interval_count();\n\n    // Free every other record -> many small free holes, no large hole.\n    let mut freed = Vec::new();\n    for (i, h) in handles.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            r.free(*h).unwrap();\n            freed.push(*h);\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let page = r.page(0).unwrap();\n    let holes = page.free_interval_count();\n    assert!(\n        holes > 1,\n        \"expected fragmentation into multiple holes, got {holes}\"\n    );\n    // A new record slightly bigger than one 12-byte hole must fail with\n    // OutOfSpace even though total free bytes exceed its size.\n    let bigger = (fill_len + 4) as usize;\n    let stats = page.free_bytes();\n    assert!(\n        stats >= bigger,\n        \"aggregate free {stats} should exceed {bigger}\"\n    );\n    drop(page);\n    let before = r.stats();\n    let put_err = r.put(&payload(99, bigger));\n    assert!(\n        matches!(put_err, Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. })),\n        \"expected out-of-space in fragmented page, got {put_err:?}\"\n    );\n    // ... and it must have spilled to a new page either way? No: first-fit\n    // tries page 0 (OutOfSpace is retryable), so it appended page 1. Put\n    // succeeded above only if a new page fit; here we asserted failure for a\n    // record that also does not fit page 0 but DID fit a fresh page — meaning\n    // put appended. Re-read semantics: above we asserted an error, so a fresh\n    // page must also be too small (it is not). Re-frame the assertion below.\n    let _ = before;\n    let _ = intervals_before;\n    let _ = slots;\n}\n\n/// Same scenario, but place the oversized record *before* a fresh page is\n/// allowed by pinning allocation to page 0 through the page API, so the\n/// fragmentation/failure/merge lifecycle is unambiguous.\n#[test]\nfn fragmentation_and_merge_via_page_api() {\n    use pfa::page::Page;\n    let mut page = Page::format(0, BS).unwrap();\n\n    // Fill with 12-byte records.\n    let mut issued: Vec<(usize, u32)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut nonce = 0u64;\n    loop {\n        match page.allocate(12) {\n            Ok((s, g)) => {\n                page.write(s, g, &payload(nonce, 12)).unwrap();\n                issued.push((s, g));\n                nonce += 1;\n            }\n            Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    // Free every other record -> many holes, free region split into pieces.\n    for (i, (s, g)) in issued.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            page.free(*s, *g).unwrap();\n        }\n    }\n    page.verify_partition().unwrap();\n    let holes = page.free_interval_count();\n    assert!(holes > 1, \"expected fragmented free region, got {holes} holes\");\n    let free_total = page.free_bytes();\n\n    // A record larger than any single hole but smaller than total free fails.\n    let need = 16u16;\n    assert!((free_total as u16) > need, \"test setup: {free_total} <= {need}\");\n    assert!(matches!(\n        page.allocate(need),\n        Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. })\n    ));\n\n    // Re-allocating into one dead slot uses one of the holes (still fits 12).\n    let (s2, g2) = page.allocate(12).unwrap();\n    page.write(s2, g2, &payload(77, 12)).unwrap();\n    page.verify_partition().unwrap();\n\n    // Compaction collapses every free interval into one and the bigger record\n    // fits. Crucially, slot indices and generations are preserved.\n    let survivors: Vec<(usize, u32, Vec<u8>)> = issued\n        .iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .filter(|(i, _)| i % 2 == 1)\n        .map(|(_, (s, g))| (*s, *g, page.read(*s, *g).unwrap().to_vec()))\n        .collect();\n    let relocated = page.compact();\n    assert_eq!(page.free_interval_count(), 1, \"free region not merged\");\n    assert!(relocated > 0, \"compaction should relocate bytes\");\n    for (s, g, bytes) in &survivors {\n        assert_eq!(\n            page.read(*s, *g).unwrap(),\n            bytes.as_slice(),\n            \"valid handle must survive compaction with same payload\"\n        );\n    }\n    let (bs3, bg3) = page.allocate(need).unwrap();\n    page.write(bs3, bg3, &payload(31, need as usize)).unwrap();\n    page.verify_partition().unwrap();\n\n    // Encode/decode round-trips with rebuilt free intervals.\n    let raw = page.encode().to_vec();\n    let reloaded = Page::decode(0, &raw, BS).unwrap();\n    reloaded.verify_partition().unwrap();\n    for (s, g, bytes) in &survivors {\n        assert_eq!(reloaded.read(*s, *g).unwrap(), bytes.as_slice());\n    }\n    assert_eq!(reloaded.read(bs3, bg3).unwrap(), &payload(31, need as usize));\n}\n\n/// Double free and use-after-free are both rejected via generations.\n#[test]\nfn double_free_and_use_after_free_rejected() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    let h = r.put(b\"record-one\").unwrap();\n    r.free(h).unwrap();\n\n    // Double free.\n    match r.free(h) {\n        Err(Error::StaleHandle {\n            presented_gen,\n            current_gen,\n            ..\n        }) => {\n            assert_eq!(presented_gen, h.gen);\n            assert_eq!(current_gen, None);\n        }\n        other => panic!(\"expected stale handle, got {other:?}\"),\n    }\n    // Read after free.\n    assert!(matches!(r.get(h), Err(Error::StaleHandle { .. })));\n\n    // The slot gets recycled for a new record with a NEW generation.\n    let h2 = r.put(b\"record-two\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(h2.page, h.page);\n    assert_eq!(h2.slot, h.slot);\n    assert_ne!(h2.gen, h.gen, \"recycled slot must get a new generation\");\n    // The old handle must not read the new record's bytes.\n    match r.get(h) {\n        Err(Error::StaleHandle {\n            presented_gen,\n            current_gen: Some(cur),\n            ..\n        }) => {\n            assert_eq!(presented_gen, h.gen);\n            assert_eq!(cur, h2.gen);\n        }\n        other => panic!(\"old handle read through recycle: {other:?}\"),\n    }\n    // The new handle reads the new data.\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h2).unwrap(), b\"record-two\");\n}\n\n/// A handle that never existed (bad slot index) is rejected distinctly.\n#[test]\nfn unknown_slot_rejected() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    r.put(b\"x\").unwrap();\n    let bogus = Handle::new(0, 9999, 1);\n    assert!(matches!(\n        r.get(bogus),\n        Err(Error::NoSuchSlot { .. })\n    ));\n    let other_page = Handle::new(42, 0, 1);\n    assert!(matches!(\n        r.get(other_page),\n        Err(Error::NoSuchSlot { .. })\n    ));\n}\n\n/// Compaction preserves every live handle across reopen (persistence).\n#[test]\nfn compaction_survives_reopen() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    let keep = (0..6)\n        .map(|i| {\n            let h = r.put(&payload(100 + i, 20)).unwrap();\n            (h, payload(100 + i, 20))\n        })\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    let doomed: Vec<Handle> = (0..6)\n        .map(|i| r.put(&payload(200 + i, 20)).unwrap())\n        .collect();\n    for h in doomed {\n        r.free(h).unwrap();\n    }\n    r.compact_all().unwrap();\n    for (h, data) in &keep {\n        assert_eq!(r.get(*h).unwrap(), data.as_slice());\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n\n    let r = r.reopen_self().unwrap();\n    for (h, data) in &keep {\n        assert_eq!(r.get(*h).unwrap(), data.as_slice());\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n}\n\n/// Reference-model differential fuzz: a stream of pseudo-random operations is\n/// applied to the repository; after every step we check partition validity,\n/// space conservation, and payload identity through live handles.\n#[test]\nfn differential_against_interval_model() {\n    for seed in 1u64..=40 {\n        run_diff(seed);\n    }\n}\n\nfn run_diff(seed: u64) {\n    let mut rng = Rng::new(seed);\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    // Live records the model currently believes in: handle -> expected bytes.\n    let mut live: Vec<(Handle, Vec<u8>)> = Vec::new();\n    // All handles ever freed or superseded; none may ever read again.\n    let mut stale: Vec<Handle> = Vec::new();\n\n    for step in 0..400 {\n        match rng.below(100) {\n            // 45% allocate\n            0..=44 => {\n                let len = 1 + rng.below(30) as u16;\n                let data = Acceptance test: fragmented allocation, double-free, stale handles,\n//! compaction — driven against the interval reference model.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::handle::Handle;\nuse pfa::io::MemStorage;\nuse pfa::page::{PartitionPiece, PAGE_HEADER_LEN, SLOT_LEN};\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nconst BS: u32 = 256;\n\n/// Construct an obviously fragmented page: interleaved allocations and frees\n/// leave many small free intervals; then assert the free space is genuinely\n/// unusable in aggregate until compaction merges it.\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_allocation_blocks_until_compaction() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    // Fill a page with many small records.\n    let mut handles = Vec::new();\n    let fill_len = 12u16;\n    loop {\n        match r.put(&payload(handles.len() as u64, fill_len as usize)) {\n            Ok(h) => handles.push(h),\n            Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) | Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let slots = r.page(0).unwrap().slot_count();\n    let intervals_before = r.page(0).unwrap().free_interval_count();\n\n    // Free every other record -> many small free holes, no large hole.\n    let mut freed = Vec::new();\n    for (i, h) in handles.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            r.free(*h).unwrap();\n            freed.push(*h);\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let page = r.page(0).unwrap();\n    let holes = page.free_interval_count();\n    assert!(\n        holes > 1,\n        \"expected fragmentation into multiple holes, got {holes}\"\n    );\n    // A new record slightly bigger than one 12-byte hole must fail with\n    // OutOfSpace even though total free bytes exceed its size.\n    let bigger = (fill_len + 4) as usize;\n    let stats = page.free_bytes();\n    assert!(\n        stats >= bigger,\n        \"aggregate free {stats} should exceed {bigger}\"\n    );\n    drop(page);\n    let before = r.stats();\n    let put_err = r.put(&payload(99, bigger));\n    assert!(\n        matches!(put_err, Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. })),\n        \"expected out-of-space in fragmented page, got {put_err:?}\"\n    );\n    // ... and it must have spilled to a new page either way? No: first-fit\n    // tries page 0 (OutOfSpace is retryable), so it appended page 1. Put\n    // succeeded above only if a new page fit; here we asserted failure for a\n    // record that also does not fit page 0 but DID fit a fresh page — meaning\n    // put appended. Re-read semantics: above we asserted an error, so a fresh\n    // page must also be too small (it is not). Re-frame the assertion below.\n    let _ = before;\n    let _ = intervals_before;\n    let _ = slots;\n}\n\n/// Same scenario, but place the oversized record *before* a fresh page is\n/// allowed by pinning allocation to page 0 through the page API, so the\n/// fragmentation/failure/merge lifecycle is unambiguous.\n#[test]\nfn fragmentation_and_merge_via_page_api() {\n    use pfa::page::Page;\n    let mut page = Page::format(0, BS).unwrap();\n\n    // Fill with 12-byte records.\n    let mut issued: Vec<(usize, u32)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut nonce = 0u64;\n    loop {\n        match page.allocate(12) {\n            Ok((s, g)) => {\n                page.write(s, g, &payload(nonce, 12)).unwrap();\n                issued.push((s, g));\n                nonce += 1;\n            }\n            Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    // Free every other record -> many holes, free region split into pieces.\n    for (i, (s, g)) in issued.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            page.free(*s, *g).unwrap();\n        }\n    }\n    page.verify_partition().unwrap();\n    let holes = page.free_interval_count();\n    assert!(holes > 1, \"expected fragmented free region, got {holes} holes\");\n    let free_total = page.free_bytes();\n\n    // A record larger than any single hole but smaller than total free fails.\n    let need = 16u16;\n    assert!((free_total as u16) > need, \"test setup: {free_total} <= {need}\");\n    assert!(matches!(\n        page.allocate(need),\n        Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. })\n    ));\n\n    // Re-allocating into one dead slot uses one of the holes (still fits 12).\n    let (s2, g2) = page.allocate(12).unwrap();\n    page.write(s2, g2, &payload(77, 12)).unwrap();\n    page.verify_partition().unwrap();\n\n    // Compaction collapses every free interval into one and the bigger record\n    // fits. Crucially, slot indices and generations are preserved.\n    let survivors: Vec<(usize, u32, Vec<u8>)> = issued\n        .iter()\n        .enumerate()\n        .filter(|(i, _)| i % 2 == 1)\n        .map(|(_, (s, g))| (*s, *g, page.read(*s, *g).unwrap().to_vec()))\n        .collect();\n    let relocated = page.compact();\n    assert_eq!(page.free_interval_count(), 1, \"free region not merged\");\n    assert!(relocated > 0, \"compaction should relocate bytes\");\n    for (s, g, bytes) in &survivors {\n        assert_eq!(\n            page.read(*s, *g).unwrap(),\n            bytes.as_slice(),\n            \"valid handle must survive compaction with same payload\"\n        );\n    }\n    let (bs3, bg3) = page.allocate(need).unwrap();\n    page.write(bs3, bg3, &payload(31, {"parentUuid":"ecd90d30-f20a-4abd-ab32-c77d9b5348c2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_td43t1t3ffxwzxxro36c2any","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/tests/acceptance.rs","old_string":"const BS: u32 = 256;\n\n/// Construct an obviously fragmented page: interleaved allocations and frees\n/// leave many small free intervals; then assert the free space is genuinely\n/// unusable in aggregate until compaction merges it.\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_allocation_blocks_until_compaction() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    // Fill a page with many small records.\n    let mut handles = Vec::new();\n    let fill_len = 12u16;\n    loop {\n        match r.put(&payload(handles.len() as u64, fill_len as usize)) {\n            Ok(h) => handles.push(h),\n            Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) | Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let slots = r.page(0).unwrap().slot_count();\n    let intervals_before = r.page(0).unwrap().free_interval_count();\n\n    // Free every other record -> many small free holes, no large hole.\n    let mut freed = Vec::new();\n    for (i, h) in handles.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            r.free(*h).unwrap();\n            freed.push(*h);\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let page = r.page(0).unwrap();\n    let holes = page.free_interval_count();\n    assert!(\n        holes > 1,\n        \"expected fragmentation into multiple holes, got {holes}\"\n    );\n    // A new record slightly bigger than one 12-byte hole must fail with\n    // OutOfSpace even though total free bytes exceed its size.\n    let bigger = (fill_len + 4) as usize;\n    let stats = page.free_bytes();\n    assert!(\n        stats >= bigger,\n        \"aggregate free {stats} should exceed {bigger}\"\n    );\n    drop(page);\n    let before = r.stats();\n    let put_err = r.put(&payload(99, bigger));\n    assert!(\n        matches!(put_err, Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) | Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. })),\n        \"expected out-of-space in fragmented page, got {put_err:?}\"\n    );\n    // ... and it must have spilled to a new page either way? No: first-fit\n    // tries page 0 (OutOfSpace is retryable), so it appended page 1. Put\n    // succeeded above only if a new page fit; here we asserted failure for a\n    // record that also does not fit page 0 but DID fit a fresh page — meaning\n    // put appended. Re-read semantics: above we asserted an error, so a fresh\n    // page must also be too small (it is not). Re-frame the assertion below.\n    let _ = before;\n    let _ = intervals_before;\n    let _ = slots;\n}","new_string":"const BS: u32 = 256;\n\n/// Repository-level fragmentation: after interleaved frees the free bytes are\n/// spread across many intervals. Allocation still succeeds (first-fit spills\n/// onto a fresh page), but the fragmented page's *largest* interval is far\n/// smaller than its total free bytes, and compaction of that page restores a\n/// single interval without invalidating any live handle.\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_allocation_then_compaction() {\n    let mut r = Repository::create(MemStorage::new(BS), BS).unwrap();\n    let mut handles = Vec::new();\n    loop {\n        match r.put(&payload(handles.len() as u64, 12)) {\n            Ok(h) => handles.push(h),\n            Err(Error::RecordTooLarge { .. }) | Err(Error::OutOfSpace { .. }) => break,\n            Err(e) => panic!(\"unexpected {e:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n    let only_page = r.page_count();\n    assert_eq!(only_page, 1);\n\n    // Free every other record -> many small free holes.\n    let mut survivors = Vec::new();\n    for (i, h) in handles.iter().enumerate() {\n        if i % 2 == 0 {\n            r.free(*h).unwrap();\n        } else {\n            survivors.push((*h, r.get(*h).unwrap()));\n        }\n    }\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    let page0 = r.page(0).unwrap();\n    let holes = page0.free_interval_count();\n    let free_total = page0.free_bytes();\n    let largest = {\n        let mut best = 0usize;\n        let mut cur = 0usize;\n        for p in page0.partition_snapshot() {\n            if let PartitionPiece::Free { start, end } = p {\n                cur = (end - start) as usize;\n                best = best.max(cur);\n            }\n        }\n        best\n    };\n    drop(page0);\n    assert!(holes > 1, \"expected multiple holes, got {holes}\");\n    assert!(\n        largest < free_total,\n        \"fragmentation: largest hole {largest} should be < total free {free_total}\"\n    );\n\n    // Compaction merges everything into one interval, handles still valid.\n    let relocated = r.compact_page(0).unwrap();\n    assert!(relocated > 0);\n    assert_eq!(r.page(0).unwrap().free_interval_count(), 1);\n    for (h, bytes) in &survivors {\n        assert_eq!(&r.get(*h).unwrap(), bytes);\n    }\n    assert_space_accounting(&r);\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n}"},"name":"Edit","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_b9a42877c25a85dc9823e3da","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":4811,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":77624,"output_tokens":1584,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"2c1b2994-23a4-4a45-b979-3c67a179da70","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:20:57.974Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

{"parentUuid":"2e93a60c-c82e-4abb-a405-0fec4d535abb","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_kmjh106e9zmuq6j77a3pmvg5","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b/tests/faults.rs","content":"//! Fault-injection tests: simulated disk errors, corrupted/torn pages and\n//! fsync failures, delivered through the injectable I/O layer.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::io::{FaultKind, FaultOp, FaultyStorage, MemStorage};\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nconst BS: u32 = 256;\n\nfn faulty() -> (\n    Repository<FaultyStorage>,\n    std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<pfa::io::FaultPolicy>>,\n) {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    // create() itself performs the header write + sync; no faults scheduled.\n    let repo = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    (repo, policy)\n}\n\n/// An injected write failure on a mutation propagates as an I/O error.\n#[test]\nfn injected_write_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.put(b\"first\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Write, \"simulated write failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"second\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// An injected sync failure propagates (the durability boundary is real).\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"simulated fsync failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"synced?\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// With durability disabled, injected sync faults do not affect correctness\n/// (the sync boundary is opt-out for tests/batch ingestion).\n#[test]\nfn no_sync_mode_ignores_sync_faults() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"should never be observed\");\n    let h = r.put(b\"batched\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h).unwrap(), b\"batched\");\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in a persisted page is detected by CRC on reopen as\n/// [`Error::Corrupt`] rather than being read as data.\n#[test]\nfn torn_page_detected_by_crc_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false); // avoid the post-write fsync fault timing\n    r.put(b\"alpha-record\").unwrap();\n    // Corrupt one byte inside the next page write's record area.\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(100);\n    let h2 = r.put(b\"beta-record\").unwrap();\n    let _ = h2;\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    match reopened {\n        Err(Error::Corrupt(msg)) => {\n            assert!(msg.contains(\"CRC\"), \"unexpected corrupt detail: {msg}\");\n        }\n        other => panic!(\"expected CRC corruption error, got {other:?}\"),\n    }\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in the FILE HEADER is likewise detected.\n#[test]\nfn torn_header_detected_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    r.put(b\"x\").unwrap();\n    // Force a new page: appending rewrites the header first; corrupt it.\n    // Fill page 0 first.\n    loop {\n        if r.put(&[0u8; 30]).is_err() {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(5);\n    // The next put that needs a new page writes header block then page block.\n    let _ = r.put(&[0u8; 5]);\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    assert!(\n        matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Corrupt(_))),\n        \"expected header corruption detection, got {reopened:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// A read fault during reopen propagates as I/O (missing/torn block).\n#[test]\nfn read_fault_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.put(b\"persisted\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Read, \"simulated read failure\");\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    // The very first read is the header block.\n    assert!(matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {reopened:?}\");\n}\n\n/// After a failed write the in-memory repository stays internally consistent:\n/// subsequent successful operations still satisfy the reference model.\n#[test]\nfn consistency_after_failed_write() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    let h1 = r.put(b\"keep-me\").unwrap();\n    policy.lock().unwrap().schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n        op: FaultOp::Write,\n        after: 0,\n        kind: FaultKind::Error(\"one bad write\".into()),\n    });\n    // This put fails at the persistence step.\n    let _ = r.put(b\"will-fail\");\n    // The allocator state did mutate in memory before the failed write; that\n    // is an accepted semantic (the write boundary is the durability point),\n    // but the in-memory partition must still be internally valid and live\n    // handles must still read correctly.\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h1).unwrap(), b\"keep-me\");\n    let h3 = r.put(b\"after-failure\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h3).unwrap(), b\"after-failure\");\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n}\n\n/// Faults scheduled with `after` counters fire at the right time.\n#[test]\nfn fault_after_counter() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    // Fail the 3rd subsequent write, not the next.\n    {\n        let mut p = policy.lock().unwrap();\n        p.schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n            op: FaultOp::Write,\n            after: 2,\n            kind: FaultKind::Error(\"third write\".into()),\n        });\n    }\n    assert!(r.put(b\"one\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"two\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"three\").is_err());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"four\").is_ok());\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_90eeddc6c53716c185467d20","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":2277,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":81720,"output_tokens":2234,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"type":"assistant","uuid":"2ea2f80b-fef7-4048-ae98-70a6d5c5c81b","timestamp":"2026-09-22T16:21:53.929Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp9/b","sessionId":"da54941b-fa48-46ef-973e-ac5b8af93c82","version":"2.1.197","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp9-b","slug":"sleepy-tinkering-mccarthy"}

Fault-injection tests: simulated disk errors, corrupted/torn pages and\n//! fsync failures, delivered through the injectable I/O layer.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse pfa::err::Error;\nuse pfa::io::{FaultKind, FaultOp, FaultyStorage, MemStorage};\nuse pfa::repo::Repository;\n\nconst BS: u32 = 256;\n\nfn faulty() -> (\n    Repository<FaultyStorage>,\n    std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<pfa::io::FaultPolicy>>,\n) {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    // create() itself performs the header write + sync; no faults scheduled.\n    let repo = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    (repo, policy)\n}\n\n/// An injected write failure on a mutation propagates as an I/O error.\n#[test]\nfn injected_write_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.put(b\"first\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Write, \"simulated write failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"second\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// An injected sync failure propagates (the durability boundary is real).\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"simulated fsync failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"synced?\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// With durability disabled, injected sync faults do not affect correctness\n/// (the sync boundary is opt-out for tests/batch ingestion).\n#[test]\nfn no_sync_mode_ignores_sync_faults() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"should never be observed\");\n    let h = r.put(b\"batched\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h).unwrap(), b\"batched\");\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in a persisted page is detected by CRC on reopen as\n/// [`Error::Corrupt`] rather than being read as data.\n#[test]\nfn torn_page_detected_by_crc_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false); // avoid the post-write fsync fault timing\n    r.put(b\"alpha-record\").unwrap();\n    // Corrupt one byte inside the next page write's record area.\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(100);\n    let h2 = r.put(b\"beta-record\").unwrap();\n    let _ = h2;\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    match reopened {\n        Err(Error::Corrupt(msg)) => {\n            assert!(msg.contains(\"CRC\"), \"unexpected corrupt detail: {msg}\");\n        }\n        other => panic!(\"expected CRC corruption error, got {other:?}\"),\n    }\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in the FILE HEADER is likewise detected.\n#[test]\nfn torn_header_detected_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    r.put(b\"x\").unwrap();\n    // Force a new page: appending rewrites the header first; corrupt it.\n    // Fill page 0 first.\n    loop {\n        if r.put(&[0u8; 30]).is_err() {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(5);\n    // The next put that needs a new page writes header block then page block.\n    let _ = r.put(&[0u8; 5]);\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    assert!(\n        matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Corrupt(_))),\n        \"expected header corruption detection, got {reopened:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// A read fault during reopen propagates as I/O (missing/torn block).\n#[test]\nfn read_fault_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.put(b\"persisted\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Read, \"simulated read failure\");\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    // The very first read is the header block.\n    assert!(matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {reopened:?}\");\n}\n\n/// After a failed write the in-memory repository stays internally consistent:\n/// subsequent successful operations still satisfy the reference model.\n#[test]\nfn consistency_after_failed_write() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    let h1 = r.put(b\"keep-me\").unwrap();\n    policy.lock().unwrap().schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n        op: FaultOp::Write,\n        after: 0,\n        kind: FaultKind::Error(\"one bad write\".into()),\n    });\n    // This put fails at the persistence step.\n    let _ = r.put(b\"will-fail\");\n    // The allocator state did mutate in memory before the failed write; that\n    // is an accepted semantic (the write boundary is the durability point),\n    // but the in-memory partition must still be internally valid and live\n    // handles must still read correctly.\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h1).unwrap(), b\"keep-me\");\n    let h3 = r.put(b\"after-failure\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h3).unwrap(), b\"after-failure\");\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n}\n\n/// Faults scheduled with `after` counters fire at the right time.\n#[test]\nfn fault_after_counter() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    // Fail the 3rd subsequent write, not the next.\n    {\n        let mut p = policy.lock().unwrap();\n        p.schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n            op: FaultOp::Write,\n            after: 2,\n            kind: FaultKind::Error(\"third write\".into()),\n        });\n    }\n    assert!(r.put(b\"one\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"two\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"three\").is_err());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"four\").is_ok());\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":88,"oldLines":17,"newStart":88,"newLines":23,"lines":["     let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));","     let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();","     r.set_durable(false);","-    r.put(b\"x\").unwrap();","-    // Force a new page: appending rewrites the header first; 30]).is_err() {","             break;","         }","     }","+    assert!(r.page_count() >= 2, \"test setup should have appended a page\");","     policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(5);","-    // The next put that needs a new page writes header block then page block.","-    let _ = r.put(&[0u8; 5]);","+    // Free a page-1 record then trigger another header rewrite by forcing a","+    // new page allocation: fill page 1 up and put once more.","+    while r.page_count() == 2 {","+        if r.put(&[0u8; no faults scheduled.\n    let repo = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    (repo, policy)\n}\n\n/// An injected write failure on a mutation propagates as an I/O error.\n#[test]\nfn injected_write_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.put(b\"first\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Write, \"simulated write failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"second\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// An injected sync failure propagates (the durability boundary is real).\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_error_propagates() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"simulated fsync failure\");\n    let err = r.put(b\"synced?\");\n    assert!(matches!(err, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {err:?}\");\n}\n\n/// With durability disabled, injected sync faults do not affect correctness\n/// (the sync boundary is opt-out for tests/batch ingestion).\n#[test]\nfn no_sync_mode_ignores_sync_faults() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Sync, \"should never be observed\");\n    let h = r.put(b\"batched\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h).unwrap(), b\"batched\");\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in a persisted page is detected by CRC on reopen as\n/// [`Error::Corrupt`] rather than being read as data.\n#[test]\nfn torn_page_detected_by_crc_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false); // avoid the post-write fsync fault timing\n    r.put(b\"alpha-record\").unwrap();\n    // Corrupt one byte inside the next page write's record area.\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(100);\n    let h2 = r.put(b\"beta-record\").unwrap();\n    let _ = h2;\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    match reopened {\n        Err(Error::Corrupt(msg)) => {\n            assert!(msg.contains(\"CRC\"), \"unexpected corrupt detail: {msg}\");\n        }\n        other => panic!(\"expected CRC corruption error, got {other:?}\"),\n    }\n}\n\n/// A bit flip in the FILE HEADER is likewise detected.\n#[test]\nfn torn_header_detected_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    // Fill page 0 with 30-byte records (a fresh page holds exactly five of\n    // them alongside their slots); the sixth forces a new page, which writes\n    // the header block first.\n    while r.page_count() == 1 {\n        if r.put(&[0u8; 30]).is_err() {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(r.page_count() >= 2, \"test setup should have appended a page\");\n    policy.lock().unwrap().corrupt_next_write(5);\n    // Free a page-1 record then trigger another header rewrite by forcing a\n    // new page allocation: fill page 1 up and put once more.\n    while r.page_count() == 2 {\n        if r.put(&[0u8; 30]).is_err() {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    assert!(\n        matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Corrupt(_))),\n        \"expected header corruption detection, got {reopened:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// A read fault during reopen propagates as I/O (missing/torn block).\n#[test]\nfn read_fault_on_reopen() {\n    let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));\n    let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();\n    r.put(b\"persisted\").unwrap();\n    policy\n        .lock()\n        .unwrap()\n        .fail_next(FaultOp::Read, \"simulated read failure\");\n    let storage = r.into_storage();\n    let reopened = Repository::open(storage, BS);\n    // The very first read is the header block.\n    assert!(matches!(reopened, Err(Error::Io(_))), \"got {reopened:?}\");\n}\n\n/// After a failed write the in-memory repository stays internally consistent:\n/// subsequent successful operations still satisfy the reference model.\n#[test]\nfn consistency_after_failed_write() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    let h1 = r.put(b\"keep-me\").unwrap();\n    policy.lock().unwrap().schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n        op: FaultOp::Write,\n        after: 0,\n        kind: FaultKind::Error(\"one bad write\".into()),\n    });\n    // This put fails at the persistence step.\n    let _ = r.put(b\"will-fail\");\n    // The allocator state did mutate in memory before the failed write; that\n    // is an accepted semantic (the write boundary is the durability point),\n    // but the in-memory partition must still be internally valid and live\n    // handles must still read correctly.\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h1).unwrap(), b\"keep-me\");\n    let h3 = r.put(b\"after-failure\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(r.get(h3).unwrap(), b\"after-failure\");\n    assert_partitions(&r);\n}\n\n/// Faults scheduled with `after` counters fire at the right time.\n#[test]\nfn fault_after_counter() {\n    let (mut r, policy) = faulty();\n    r.set_durable(false);\n    // Fail the 3rd subsequent write, not the next.\n    {\n        let mut p = policy.lock().unwrap();\n        p.schedule(pfa::io::Fault {\n            op: FaultOp::Write,\n            after: 2,\n            kind: FaultKind::Error(\"third write\".into()),\n        });\n    }\n    assert!(r.put(b\"one\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"two\").is_ok());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"three\").is_err());\n    assert!(r.put(b\"four\").is_ok());\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":88,"oldLines":29,"newStart":88,"newLines":31,"lines":["     let (st, policy) = FaultyStorage::wrap(MemStorage::new(BS));","     let mut r = Repository::create(st, BS).unwrap();","     r.set_durable(false);","-    // Fill page 0 with 30-byte records (a fresh page holds exactly five of","-    // them alongside their slots);
